definition_en: A rod-shaped bacterium; with a capital, a genus of such bacteria that form resistant spores.
core_image: 显微镜下一根根短棒似的小东西
scene: 培养皿里那株杆菌一夜之间铺满了培养基。 The bacillus in the dish had covered the medium overnight.

senses.title: Any rod-shaped bacterium
senses.definition: a bacterium whose cell is shaped like a short rod, whatever its species
senses.definitionCN: 细胞形如短棒的细菌，不论其种类
senses.example: The smear showed a few bacilli.
senses.exampleCN: 涂片显示有少量杆菌。
senses.why: Bacillus is Latin for a little rod, so the name describes the shape seen under the lens, not the disease.
senses.whyCN: bacillus 在拉丁语中意为「小棒」，因此这个名字描述镜下所见的形状，而非疾病。

senses.title: The spore-forming genus
senses.definition: with a capital, a genus of rod-shaped bacteria that form spores able to survive heat and drying
senses.definitionCN: 大写时指一个杆状细菌属，能形成耐热耐干的孢子
senses.example: Bacillus spores survive boiling for minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 芽孢杆菌的孢子能在沸水中存活数分钟。
senses.why: Once microbiology needed exact genera, the shape word was fixed as a formal name for one group.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学需要精确的属名之后，这个形状词就被定为某一群的正式名称。

intro.en: Bacillus is Late Latin bacillus, a little rod, a diminutive of Latin baculus, a stick or staff; the plural bacilli keeps the Latin pattern.
intro.cn: bacillus 是晚期拉丁语 bacillus「小棒」，为拉丁语 baculus「棍、杖」的指小形式；复数 bacilli 保留拉丁语变化。

items.en: A root meaning a staff or support stands behind words for sticks and props.
items.cn: 一个表示「杖、支撑」的词根支撑着棍棒与支柱类的词。

items.en: Latin baculus meant a stick or walking staff, the plain word for a rod.
items.cn: 拉丁语 baculus 意为「棍、手杖」，是指杆的普通词。

items.en: The diminutive bacillus meant a little rod, used for small slender objects.
items.cn: 指小形式 bacillus 意为「小棒」，用于细长的物件。

items.en: Naturalists used bacillus for rod-shaped organisms seen under early microscopes.
items.cn: 博物学者用 bacillus 指早期显微镜下所见的杆状生物。

items.en: Bacteriology fixed Bacillus as a genus of spore-forming rods in the 1870s.
items.cn: 细菌学在 1870 年代把 Bacillus 定为产芽孢杆菌的一个属。

items.en: English kept the Latin plural bacilli, and the word entered public health writing.
items.cn: 英语保留拉丁语复数 bacilli，这个词也进入公共卫生文献。

definition_zh: 自我控制；自制力；镇定；[工程] 自控（系统对自身的控制）
definition_en: the ability to hold back one's impulses and keep one's behaviour in order
core_image: 一个人左手握住右手手腕，把已经伸向糖罐的手拉回来
scene: 甜品台前，孩子的手伸出去又缩回来， Her self-control kept her from taking a third cake.
sceneCN: 这里 self-control 指「克制自己欲望的能力」（第 1 个义项：抑制自身冲动的能力）；句意为她的自制力让她没有拿第三块蛋糕。图中可辨识物件：甜品台、蛋糕、缩回的手、餐巾。

pos.zh: 自我控制；自制力；镇定；自控（工程用语）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次自控表现）

senses.title: The ability to hold back one's impulses
senses.definition: the ability to stop oneself from acting on a strong urge
senses.definitionCN: 阻止自己凭强烈欲望行动的能力
senses.example: Her self-control kept her from taking a third cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她的自制力让她没有拿第三块蛋糕。
senses.why: Self names the same person as both the one who wants and the one who holds back, so the control runs in a loop.
senses.whyCN: self 让同一个人既是想要的人，也是拉住的人，因此这种控制在一个人身上绕成环。

senses.title: Composure under provocation
senses.definition: the ability to stay calm when someone tries to provoke or upset you
senses.definitionCN: 在别人试图激怒或扰乱你时保持平静的能力
senses.example: He answered the insult with self-control.
senses.exampleCN: 他以镇定回应那句侮辱。
senses.why: Holding back an impulse is most visible when the impulse is anger, and then the word names composure.
senses.whyCN: 当被克制的冲动是愤怒时，克制最容易被看见，这时这个词命名的是镇定。

senses.title: Self-regulation studied in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学研究的自我调节
senses.definition: in psychology, the capacity to regulate one's own attention, emotion and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，调节自身注意、情绪与行为的能力
senses.example: The study links self-control to long-term outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把自我控制与长期结果联系起来。
senses.why: Psychology treats the loop as a capacity that can be trained and measured.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这个环看成一种可以训练、可以测量的能力。

senses.title: Resisting a temptation
senses.definition: the act of refusing something attractive that is within reach
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝某件近在手边、颇具吸引力之物的行为
senses.example: Self-control at the checkout is hardest of all.
senses.exampleCN: 在收银台前的自制最难。
senses.why: The general capacity is tested at particular points, and the word can name the test itself.
senses.whyCN: 一般的能力在具体节点上受检验，这个词也可以命名那次检验。

senses.title: Discipline in performance
senses.definition: the discipline that keeps a performer within a chosen technique
senses.definitionCN: 使表演者留在既定技艺范围里的自律
senses.example: Her self-control on stage never shows in the playing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在台上的自律从不在演奏中显露出来。
senses.why: Artistic restraint is the same holding back, applied to a technique rather than to a desire.
senses.whyCN: 艺术上的克制是同一种拉住，只是对象是技艺而不是欲望。

senses.title: Moral or ascetic restraint
senses.definition: the moral discipline of denying oneself permitted pleasures
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝自己本可享受的乐趣的道德自律
senses.example: The rule was meant to teach self-control, not shame.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规矩意在教人自律，而不是使人羞愧。
senses.why: Religious and moral traditions treat the loop as the training ground of character.
senses.whyCN: 宗教与道德传统把这个环当作性格的训练场。

senses.title: A system controlling itself, in engineering
senses.titleCN: 工程学中系统对自身的控制
senses.definition: in engineering, the regulation of a system by its own feedback rather than by an outside operator
senses.definitionCN: 工程学中，系统靠自身反馈而非外部操作者来调节
senses.example: The thermostat gives the furnace a simple self-control.
senses.exampleCN: 恒温器让锅炉具备一种简单的自控。
senses.why: The loop that runs in a person also runs in a machine: output is fed back to adjust input.
senses.whyCN: 在人身上绕成环的东西，在机器里也绕成环：输出被送回以调整输入。

senses.title: Governing the self as a system
senses.titleCN: 把自我当作系统来治理
senses.definition: the abstract idea of the self as both governor and governed
senses.definitionCN: 把自我同时看成治理者与被治理者的抽象观念
senses.example: The essay treats self-control as a constitution written inside one mind.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把自制看成一部位于单一心灵内部的宪法。
senses.why: Once the loop is seen whole, it becomes a model of the self as a governed system.
senses.whyCN: 当这个环被整体看见时，它就成了「自我作为被治理系统」的模型。

intro.en: Self-control joins the native pronoun self with control, a word borrowed from Medieval Latin contrarotulus, a counter-roll kept for checking accounts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: self-control 把本族语代词 self 与 control 组合起来；control 借自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus，指用来核对账目的对照卷。年代均为约数。

items.en: Self began as a pronoun and adjective meaning the same person, and it has always been able to form compounds with nouns.
items.cn: self 起初是代词兼形容词，指「同一个人」，一直都能与名词构成复合词。

items.en: Contrarotulus joined contra meaning against and rotulus meaning a roll, and it named a duplicate roll kept to check an account.
items.cn: contrarotulus 由 contra「对着」与 rotulus「卷」构成，指用来核对账目的副本卷。

items.en: The word passed through Old French as contrerolle and into English as control, first meaning a check or a register.
items.cn: 这个词经古法语 contrerolle 进入英语作 control，最初指核对或登记册。

items.en: By the sixteenth century control had widened from checking a record to directing or restraining anything.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，control 已从核对记录扩展到指挥或约束任何事情。

items.en: Self-control appeared in the early eighteenth century as the power of controlling one's own actions and desires.
items.cn: self-control 在十八世纪初出现，指控制自身行为与欲望的力量。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation for the compound is not fixed, and the deeper origin of rotulus beyond its diminutive form is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词的最早英语书证年代无定论；rotulus 在指小形式之外的更深来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group shares wording with self-control or its second element; the second holds nouns for holding back. The self- element is what separates the first entry from the rest.
note.cn: 第一组与 self-control 或其第二部分共用词形；第二组是表示克制的名词。self- 这一部分正是第一条与其余各条的分界。

entries.definition: Holding oneself back from action; it stresses not doing something, while self-control also covers keeping order and staying calm.
entries.definitionCN: 拉住自己不去行动；它强调「不做」，而 self-control 还涵盖维持秩序与保持镇定。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a person who has self-control.
entries.definitionCN: 描述具有自制力之人的形容词。

entries.definition: Direction or restraint of something; without self- it usually points to power over other people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的指挥或约束；不带 self- 时通常指对他者或他物的权力。

entries.definition: The value one places on oneself; the self- is the same, but the second element concerns judgement, not restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对自己的评价；self- 相同，但第二部分涉及判断，而不是克制。

entries.definition: The strength of deliberate intention; self-control is the holding back, willpower is the force that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 有意的决心所带的强度；self-control 是那个拉住的动作，willpower 是拉住它的力量。

entries.definition: Order produced by training or rule; self-control is the inner capacity, discipline often the outward habit.
entries.definitionCN: 经由训练或规则产生的秩序；self-control 是内在能力，discipline 常指外在习惯。

entries.definition: A calm appearance under pressure; it covers the look of control rather than the whole capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 压力下的平静外表；它涵盖的是控制的外观，而不是整套能力。

entries.definition: The act or habit of holding back; it can also name an external limit, which self-control cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 拉住自己的行为或习惯；它也能指外部限制，而 self-control 不能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, the real phrase family and the technical sense that keeps the same loop.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个复合词真实的两半、真实的搭配家族，以及保留同一个环的技术义。

normal.en: Self plus control: the same person is both the one who wants and the one who says no.
normal.cn: self 加 control：同一个人既是要的那个人，也是说不的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs self-control, self-controlled, self-controlling and control.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 self-control（自制）、self-controlled（有自制力的）、self-controlling（自我控制的）、control（控制）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: exercise self-control, lose self-control, a model of self-control.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：运用自制力、失去自制、自制力的典范。

normal.en: Control itself came from a counter-roll kept to check accounts, so the oldest image is a second record that catches an error.
normal.cn: control 本身来自用来核对账目的对照卷，因此最古老的画面是一份能查出错误的第二记录。

normal.en: Engineering uses the same compound for a system that regulates itself by feedback.
normal.cn: 工程学用同一个复合词指靠反馈自我调节的系统。

examples.en: The training programme builds self-control in young athletes.

examples.en: The valve gives the tank a measure of self-control.
examples.cn: 这个阀门让储罐具备一定程度的自控。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loop: the same person both wants and refuses, and that loop is then applied to anger, to psychology, to a single temptation, to technique, to morals, to a machine and finally to the self seen as a governed system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个环展开：同一个人既想要又拒绝；这个环再依次用于愤怒、心理学、一次具体的诱惑、技艺、道德、机器，最后用于被看成被治理系统的自我。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand closing over the other wrist and pulling the reaching hand back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握住另一只手的手腕，把已经伸出去的手拉回来。

branches.en: IMPULSE AND TEMPTATION: the general capacity is tested at one tempting object.
branches.cn: 冲动与诱惑：一般的能力在一件诱人的东西上受检验。

branches.en: COMPOSURE AND MORAL: holding back anger and denying a permitted pleasure use the same grip.
branches.cn: 镇定与道德：压住怒气与拒绝本可享受的乐趣，用的是同一种握力。

branches.en: REGULATION AND TECHNIQUE: psychology measures the loop, and performance keeps within it.
branches.cn: 调节与技艺：心理学测量这个环，表演则留在环内。

branches.en: MACHINE: feedback makes a system its own governor.
branches.cn: 机器：反馈让系统成为自己的治理者。

branches.en: SELF AS STATE: the whole loop becomes a constitution inside one mind.
branches.cn: 自我如国：整个环变成一部写在单颗心里的宪法。

intro.en: Self-control is a native pronoun joined to a borrowed noun, and each half can be read on its own.

latinIntro.en: The second half comes from Medieval Latin contrarotulus, built on contra meaning against and rotulus meaning a roll; the same stock gives controller and the verb control.
latinIntro.cn: 后半部分来自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus，由 contra「对着」与 rotulus「卷」构成；同一词干衍生 controller 与动词 control。

senses.title: Money held in other countries' currencies
senses.titleCN: 以他国货币持有的资金
senses.definition: currency that is not the legal tender of the holder's own country
senses.definitionCN: 非持有者本国法定货币的货币
senses.example: The exporter kept part of its earnings in foreign exchange rather than converting at once.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商把部分收入以外汇形式留存，没有立即兑换。
senses.why: foreign marks what is outside the home currency, and exchange marks the swap, so the phrase names money that must be swapped before it can be used at home.
senses.whyCN: 「外国的」标出本国货币之外，「交换」标出兑换，整个短语指必须先换过才能在国内使用的钱。

senses.title: The interbank currency market
senses.definition: the global network of dealers and platforms where currencies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 交易商与平台在全球买卖货币的网络
senses.example: Turnover in foreign exchange exceeds that of every other financial market.
senses.exampleCN: 外汇市场的成交额超过其他任何金融市场。
senses.why: many dealers and platforms quote at once, so the sum of their trades becomes a market rather than a single swap.
senses.whyCN: 许多交易商与平台同时报价，他们交易的总和于是成为一个市场，而非一次单独的交换。

senses.title: Reserves held by a monetary authority
senses.titleCN: 货币当局持有的外汇储备
senses.definition: the stock of foreign currency and claims a central bank keeps to defend its own money
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行为捍卫本国货币而持有的外币与债权存量
senses.example: The bank spent a fifth of its foreign exchange to slow the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 该央行动用了五分之一的外汇储备来减缓跌势。
senses.why: a central bank must hold foreign money to intervene, so the phrase also names the stock it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 央行必须持有外国货币才能干预，因此这个短语也指它所存的存量。

senses.title: A settlement or conversion transaction
senses.definition: the actual operation of buying, selling or settling a foreign currency payment
senses.definitionCN: 买入、卖出或结算外币支付的实际操作
senses.example: The invoice was settled by a foreign exchange transfer through two banks.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔发票通过两家银行的外汇转账结算。
senses.why: the abstract money becomes a concrete operation when an invoice has to be paid across a border.
senses.whyCN: 当一张发票需要跨境支付时，抽象的外币就变成一次具体操作。

senses.title: Earnings received in foreign currency
senses.definition: export revenue or other income that arrives in a currency other than the home one
senses.definitionCN: 以非本国货币到账的出口收入或其他收入
senses.example: Tourism is the island's main source of foreign exchange.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是该岛主要的外汇收入来源。
senses.why: exporters and hosts receive payment in the buyer's currency, so the phrase also names the inflow.
senses.whyCN: 出口商与接待方收取买方货币的付款，因此这个短语也指流入的那一笔。

senses.title: Exposure to currency movements
senses.definition: the risk that a change in currency values alters the value of a payment or holding
senses.definitionCN: 货币价值变化改变某笔支付或持有物价值的风险
senses.example: A firm with costs at home and sales abroad carries constant foreign exchange risk.
senses.exampleCN: 成本在本国、销售在国外的公司长期承担外汇风险。
senses.why: holding or owing foreign money means a price move can change the value of the position.
senses.whyCN: 持有或欠下外币，意味着价格变动能改变头寸的价值。

senses.title: Official control of currency dealings
senses.titleCN: 官方对外汇往来的管制
senses.definition: rules that limit who may hold or trade foreign currency and at what rate
senses.definitionCN: 限制何人可持有或交易外币以及按何价的规则
senses.example: During the shortage, foreign exchange was rationed by licence.
senses.exampleCN: 在短缺时期，外汇凭许可证配给。
senses.why: a state short of foreign money may forbid or license its use, which adds a legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 缺少外汇的国家可能禁止或凭许可使用它，于是添上法律义。

senses.title: A retail counter that sells currency
senses.definition: a shop or desk where travellers buy and sell foreign notes
senses.definitionCN: 旅客买卖外币现钞的店铺或柜台
senses.example: She bought euros at a foreign exchange near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近的一家外币兑换点买了欧元。
senses.why: travellers need notes in hand, so the same business appears as a counter selling paper money.
senses.whyCN: 旅客需要手头的现钞，同一业务于是表现为出售纸币的柜台。

intro.en: Foreign descends from Latin foris 'outside', by way of foranus and Old French forain; exchange comes from Latin cambiare 'to swap'. The phrase is a commercial formation of the early modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: foreign 经拉丁 foranus 与古法语 forain 上溯 foris「外面」；exchange 出自拉丁 cambiare「交换」。这个短语是近代早期的商业造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Foris meant 'outside, out of doors', and it also underlies forum, the open space outside a house. What is foreign is literally what is outside the door.
items.cn: foris 意为「外面、户外」，也是 forum（屋外空地）的来源。所谓外国的，字面上就是门外的。

items.en: The adjective foranus 'of the outside' passed into Old French as forain, and English took it as foreign in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 foranus「外面的」进入古法语作 forain，英语于 15 世纪吸收为 foreign。

items.en: Cambiare 'to barter, swap' gave Old French eschangier and English exchange; its own earlier origin is uncertain and is treated as reconstructed.
items.cn: cambiare「以物易物、交换」给出古法语 eschangier 与英语 exchange；它更早的来源不确定，按重构处理。

items.en: From the fourteenth century, a bill of exchange let a merchant pay abroad without carrying coin, and foreign exchange grew out of that trade.
items.cn: 自 14 世纪起，汇票让商人无需携带硬币即可在海外付款，外汇业务正是从这种贸易中生长出来。

items.en: The phrase foreign exchange is recorded from the seventeenth century, first for foreign bills and coin, later for the market that trades them.
items.cn: 短语 foreign exchange 见于 17 世纪，先指外国汇票与硬币，后指交易它们的市场。

items.en: The twentieth century added reserves, controls, risk and a global interbank market, each with its own vocabulary.
items.cn: 20 世纪添上储备、管制、风险与全球银行间市场，每一项都有自己的说法。

note.en: Group one holds words built on outside or on swapping; group two holds related financial terms that name other parts of the same system.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「外面」或「交换」词根的词；第二组是同一体系内指其他环节的金融术语。

entries.definition: A person from another country; the money sense belongs to the phrase, not to this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自另一国的人；货币义属于短语，而不属于这个名词。

entries.definition: A traders' shortening of the phrase, used mainly for the market rather than for banknotes.
entries.definitionCN: 交易员对短语的缩略，主要指标市场而非现钞。

entries.definition: The swap of one thing for another; adding foreign specifies that the things are currencies.
entries.definitionCN: 指一物换一物的动作；加上「外国的」才限定所换之物为货币。

entries.definition: The proportion at which two currencies swap; foreign exchange is the money and the business itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指两种货币相换的比例；外汇则是货币本身与业务本身。

entries.definition: Foreign money from a politically and economically stable country, easily accepted in trade.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自政治经济稳定国家、贸易中易被接受的外币，是外汇的一部分。

entries.definition: Money sent by a worker abroad to family at home; it is a flow of foreign exchange, not the whole stock.
entries.definitionCN: 指在外工作者寄回家人的钱；它是外汇的一种流量，而非全部存量。

entries.tag: money crossing borders for any pur
entries.definition: Movement of investment money across borders; currency exchange may or may not be involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指投资资金跨境流动；未必涉及货币兑换。

entries.definition: The national ledger of all cross-border payments; foreign exchange dealings are one line inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国全部跨境支付的账簿；外汇往来只是其中一行。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Foreign means outside the door; exchange means swap: money from outside that must be swapped.
normal.cn: 「外国的」指门外，「交换」指换，合起来就是门外来的、必须换过才能用的钱。

normal.en: The family runs foreign, foreigner, exchange, exchangeable, forex.
normal.cn: 同族词包括外国的、外国人、交换、可兑换的、外汇缩略语。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the parts of the system: market, reserves, earnings, control, risk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出体系的各部分：市场、储备、收入、管制、风险。

normal.en: A bill of exchange let a merchant pay abroad without carrying coin, which is where the business began.
normal.cn: 汇票让商人不必携带硬币就能在海外付款，业务正是从这里开始。

normal.en: Reserves are the country's saved foreign money, kept for the day its own currency needs defending.
normal.cn: 外汇储备是国家存下的外币，留着在本国货币需要捍卫的那天使用。

abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃匣装几种颜色的纸币，盖子上贴着换算表。

abstract.en: Picture a merchant in one port paying a supplier in another, with no coin travelling between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个港口的商人向另一港口的供货商付款，硬币并未在两地之间移动。

abstract.en: Picture a country's vault of foreign notes, counted each month against its own currency.
abstract.cn: 想象一国存外币的金库，每月对着本国货币盘点一次。

examples.en: The country earns most of its foreign exchange from tourism and remittances.
examples.cn: 该国的外汇收入大部分来自旅游与侨汇。

examples.en: Foreign exchange desks in the capital reported unusually heavy selling of the local currency.
examples.cn: 首都的外汇柜台报告本币出现异常大量的卖盘。

examples.en: Controls on foreign exchange made it hard for firms to pay overseas suppliers.
examples.cn: 外汇管制让企业难以向海外供货商付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外国的」加「交换」——从门外来的钱，用之前先得换成本国货币 → 外汇

root: foreign 经拉丁 foranus 上溯 foris「外面」，与 forum 同源；exchange 出自拉丁 cambiare「交换」，更深来源不确定。短语成形于 17 世纪，源自汇票贸易。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: money crosses a border, must be swapped, is traded in a market, is stored as reserves, settles an invoice, arrives as earnings, creates risk, is controlled, and is sold at a counter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个流动展开：钱越过边界，必须被交换，在市场中被交易，被存成储备，结算一张发票，作为收入到账，产生风险，受到管制，最后在柜台上被卖出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: currency from outside the door, waiting to be swapped before it can be spent at home.
core.cn: 核心意象：从门外来的货币，换过之后才能在国内花用。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE OPERATION: the stock of outside currency and the act of settling it.
branches.cn: 货币与操作：门外货币的存量，以及结算它的动作。

branches.en: THE MARKET: dealers meet to swap one currency for another at quoted prices.
branches.cn: 市场：交易商按报价把一种货币换成另一种。

branches.en: THE STATE'S HAND: reserves are what the state keeps, controls are what it forbids.
branches.cn: 国家之手：储备是国家留下的，管制是国家禁止的。

branches.en: INFLOW AND EXPOSURE: money arrives as earnings, and the same flow exposes the holder to price moves.
branches.cn: 流入与敞口：钱作为收入到账，同一流动又让持有者承受价格变动。

branches.en: THE COUNTER: the same money appears as banknotes sold to a traveller.
branches.cn: 柜台：同一笔钱以现钞形式卖给旅客。

intro.en: Both halves are old borrowings: one from a Latin word for outside, one from a Latin verb for swapping, and each brought a family of English words with it.
intro.cn: 两半都是古老借词：一半来自拉丁语「外面」，一半来自拉丁语「交换」，各自带来一族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris and foranus stand behind foreign; Latin cambiare stands behind exchange, change and interchangeable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foris 与 foranus 支撑 foreign 一族；拉丁 cambiare 支撑 exchange、change 与 interchangeable。

senses.title: The power to produce a result
senses.definition: the ability to produce the intended result
senses.definitionCN: （名词）产生预期结果的能力
senses.example: Nobody doubted the efficacy of the new seal against the damp.

intro.en: Efficacy is Latin efficacia, the power of accomplishing, built on efficax, able to accomplish, which rests on efficere, to work out.
intro.cn: efficacy 就是拉丁语 efficacia（办成事情的能力），建立在 efficax（能办成的）之上，而 efficax 又来自 efficere（做出、促成）。

items.en: Latin efficere means to work out or bring about.
items.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 意为做出、促成。

items.en: Latin efficax means able to accomplish, with the stem efficac-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 efficax 意为能办成的，词干为 efficac-。

items.en: The noun efficacia names the power of accomplishing.
items.cn: 名词 efficacia 指办成事情的能力。

items.en: English borrowed efficacy in the 14C for the power to produce an effect.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 efficacy，指产生效果的能力。

items.en: Doctors used efficacy for the strength of a remedy.
items.cn: 医生用 efficacy 指药方的效力。

items.en: Clinical trials turned vaccine efficacy into a measurable percentage.
items.cn: 临床试验使疫苗效力成为可测量的百分比。

note.en: Efficacy and efficiency share the Latin root facere, to do, but efficacy asks whether the result comes while efficiency asks how little effort it costs.
note.cn: efficacy 与 efficiency 共用拉丁词根 facere（做），但 efficacy 问结果有没有出来，efficiency 问花了多少力气。

dict_mnemonic.text: efficacy ＝ ef-（向外）＋ fic（做，拉丁 facere）＋ -acy（名词后缀，表性质）＝「能做出来的性质」。同一词根换词尾：-acious → efficacious 灵验的（形容词，常修饰药物、疗法）；-acy → efficacy 功效（名词，不可数为主）；-iency → efficiency 效率。记住这条分工：efficacy 只问「有没有用」，efficiency 还问「省不省」，effectiveness 是日常口语里最常用的「有效性」。医学语境里 efficacy 特指理想试验条件下的效力，落到真实人群则常说 effectiveness。搭配记 clinical efficacy 临床疗效、vaccine efficacy 疫苗效力、prove the efficacy 证明功效。

branches.cn: 产生结果的能力。

branches.en: The strength of a treatment.
branches.cn: 疗法的作用强度。

branches.en: The measured degree of success.
branches.cn: 被量出来的成功程度。

branches.en: Both name a power that produces an effect.
branches.cn: 两者都指能产生效果的力量。

branches.en: Both are expressed as a number.
branches.cn: 两者都用数字表达。

intro.en: Efficacy is ef- plus fic- plus -acy; -acious gives efficacious and -ency gives efficiency.
intro.cn: efficacy 由 ef- 加 fic- 加 -acy 组成；-acious 给出 efficacious，-ency 给出 efficiency。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere means to make, efficax able to accomplish and potens powerful; these roots give efficacy, efficacious and potency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 意为做，efficax 意为能办成的，potens 意为有力的；这些词根给出 efficacy、efficacious 与 potency。

efficacy, efficient
efficacy, accuracy
efficacious, tenacious

validity, valid

definition_zh: 读写能力；（某一领域的）基本素养与判断力；识字普及程度
definition_en: the ability to read and write, and the competence needed to understand and use information in a particular field
core_image: 一张旧书桌上摊开的识字课本，页边压着一支削短的铅笔，旁边是一份签过名字的登记表
scene: 夜校的桌上摊着识字课本，页边压着一支削短的铅笔。 Adult literacy classes fill the church hall on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
sceneCN: 这里指「读写能力」（第 1 个义项：读书识字的基本能力）；句意为成人识字班每逢周二和周四坐满了教堂大厅。可辨识物件：识字课本、铅笔、登记表、长桌。

pos.zh: 读写能力；素养（通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 识字的；有文化的 / 识字者

senses.title: The ability to read and write
senses.definition: the basic ability to read and write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 读懂并写出简短浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Literacy opens the first door that poverty had shut.
senses.exampleCN: 读写能力打开了贫困关上的第一道门。
senses.why: the noun was built on the Latin word for a letter of the alphabet, so its oldest content is simply knowing one's letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建在拉丁语「字母」一词上，因此它最古老的内容就是「认识字母」。

senses.title: The measured level in a population
senses.titleCN: 一个人群中被统计的识字程度
senses.definition: the share of a population that can read and write, treated as a figure to be counted
senses.definitionCN: 能够读写者在人口中所占的比例，被当作可统计的数字
senses.example: Literacy in the province rose from half to four fifths in one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个省的识字水平在一代人之内从一半升至五分之四。
senses.why: once states began to measure the skill, the word also named the number rather than the ability.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家开始测量这项技能，这个词也就指数字而非能力。

senses.title: Functional literacy for daily tasks
senses.titleCN: 应付日常事务的实用读写能力
senses.definition: the reading and writing needed to fill in forms, follow instructions and manage a household
senses.definitionCN: 填写表格、看懂指示、料理家务所需的读写能力
senses.example: The course targets functional literacy rather than exam skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课针对的是日常实用读写能力，而不是应试技巧。
senses.why: policy shifted focus from letters to use, so the old word acquired a practical measure.
senses.whyCN: 政策重心从「认字」转向「会用」，这个旧词由此带上实用尺度。

senses.title: Digital literacy
senses.titleCN: 使用数字工具与判断网络信息的能力
senses.definition: the ability to use computers and networks and to judge what one finds there
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机与网络，并判断所见信息的能力
senses.example: Students need digital literacy before they can research online.
senses.exampleCN: 学生要先具备数字素养，才能在网络上做研究。
senses.why: the pattern of basic competence in a domain was extended from print to screens.
senses.whyCN: 「某领域的基本能力」这一模式从纸面扩展到了屏幕。

senses.title: Financial literacy
senses.titleCN: 看懂收支、利率与风险的能力
senses.definition: the ability to understand money, interest, debt and risk well enough to decide wisely
senses.definitionCN: 理解金钱、利率、债务与风险并据以明智决策的能力
senses.example: Schools now teach financial literacy alongside mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 学校如今把金融素养与数学一起教。
senses.why: the same frame applies wherever a field has codes that outsiders cannot read.
senses.whyCN: 只要某领域有一套外人读不懂的规则，这个框架就适用。

senses.title: Media literacy
senses.titleCN: 识别媒体信息意图与可信度的能力
senses.definition: the ability to read how news and advertising are built, and to judge their reliability
senses.definitionCN: 看懂新闻与广告如何被构造，并判断其可信度的能力
senses.example: Media literacy helps readers notice what a headline leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体素养帮助读者察觉标题省略了什么。
senses.why: news and advertising are constructed texts, so reading them needs the same skill as reading print.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与广告都是被构造的文本，读懂它们需要与读印刷品相同的功夫。

senses.title: Cultural literacy
senses.titleCN: 共享文化常识的通晓程度
senses.definition: the shared background knowledge that lets people understand references and jokes
senses.definitionCN: 使人能理解典故与玩笑的共同背景知识
senses.example: Cultural literacy includes knowing why a certain date matters.
senses.exampleCN: 文化素养包括知道某个日期为何重要。
senses.why: the word widened from letters to the common stock of references a society assumes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「字母」扩展到社会默认人人共有的典故储备。

senses.title: Literacy in a specialized field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业领域的基本通晓
senses.definition: working knowledge of the basic ideas and vocabulary of a subject such as science or law
senses.definitionCN: 对科学、法律等学科的基本概念与术语具备可用知识
senses.example: Scientific literacy is now treated as part of general education.
senses.exampleCN: 科学素养如今被视为通识教育的一部分。
senses.why: a subject's basic vocabulary works like an alphabet, so the same word fits it.
senses.whyCN: 某学科的基本词汇就像一套字母，因此同一个词也适用于它。

intro.en: Literacy is English literate plus the noun ending -cy, and literate goes back to Latin litteratus 'lettered', built on littera 'letter of the alphabet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语形容词「识字的」上加名词后缀构成，而该形容词上溯拉丁 litteratus「识字的」，后者建于 littera「字母」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet; in the plural it also meant a written message or writings in general. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母；复数时也指书信或一般著作。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus meant 'marked with letters, lettered, learned', an adjective formed from the noun.
items.cn: litteratus 意为「写有字母的、识字的、有学问的」，是由该名词构成的形容词。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fifteenth century, using it first for learned people and later for anyone able to read.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，先用于有学问的人，后用于任何能读书的人。

items.en: The noun is a nineteenth-century formation, made as the positive counterpart of illiteracy when mass schooling made the skill a public question.
items.cn: 这个名词是十九世纪的构词，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法而造，当时大众教育使识字成为公共议题。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word was attached to new fields, giving digital, financial, media and scientific literacy.
items.cn: 从二十世纪后期起，这个词被挂到新的领域上，形成数字、金融、媒体与科学素养等说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the word for a letter is unknown, and the exact first printed use of the modern noun is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个现代名词最早的确切印刷书证亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same letter-root that are easily swapped; group two holds neighbours naming competence.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「字母」词根、容易用错的词；第二组是表示能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a person or society that can read; the noun names the ability itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能读写的个人或社会；名词则指能力本身。

entries.definition: The body of written works, or the published material on a subject; it is the product, not the ability.
entries.definitionCN: 指成体系的著作，或某主题的已发表文献；是产物而非能力。

entries.definition: Meaning 'following the exact words'; it shares the letter-root but has nothing to do with reading skill.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，虽共享「字母」词根，却与读写能力无关。

entries.definition: The lack of the ability; it is the negative noun built with a prefix of negation.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏这种能力，是用否定前缀构成的反面名词。

entries.definition: Basic competence with numbers, coined on the model of literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数字的基本能力，仿照「读写能力」造出。

entries.definition: The broad process of schooling; literacy is one measurable part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛的学校教育过程；读写能力是其中可测量的一部分。

entries.definition: A general word for a high level of skill in something; it carries no link to letters.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某项技能的高水平，不含与「字母」的联系。

entries.definition: The sufficiency to perform a task; it is broader and less measurable than literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以完成任务的能力，范围更广，且不如读写能力那样可测量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'letter', so the core of the word is literally knowing one's letters.
normal.cn: 词根意为「字母」，因此这个词的核心字面上就是「认识字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the newer fields: digital, financial and media literacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出较新的领域：数字素养、金融素养与媒体素养。

normal.en: The noun pairs with its negative twin, one built with a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 这个名词与它的否定孪生词配对，后者由否定前缀构成。

normal.en: The family runs literate, illiterate, literature, literal, literacy.
normal.cn: 同族包括「识字的」「不识字的」「文学」「字面的」「读写能力」。

normal.en: The phrase 'literacy campaign' keeps the public-policy sense visible.
normal.cn: 「扫盲运动」这一说法让公共政策义保持可见。

abstract.en: Picture a key that fits many doors but was cut for one lock first.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能开许多门的钥匙，最初却只为一把锁而削。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lets a reader walk through a dark room without falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，让读者走过暗室而不摔倒。

abstract.en: Picture a currency accepted in every shop, learned one letter at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一种每个店铺都收的货币，是一个字母一个字母学来的。

examples.en: Literacy among women rose fastest where evening classes were free.
examples.cn: 在夜校免费的地方，女性识字率上升最快。

examples.en: Digital literacy is now as basic as reading a timetable.
examples.cn: 数字素养如今已和看懂时刻表一样基础。

examples.en: The campaign cut adult illiteracy by half in six years.
examples.cn: 这场运动在六年内把成人文盲率降低了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特乐西」——里里外外认得那些特小的字母，心里就乐，这就是读写能力。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」构成形容词 litteratus「识字的」；英语先借入形容词，十九世纪再加名词后缀构成 literacy，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one seed: knowing letters becomes the ability to read, then a number to count, then a set of practical competences that spread to screens, money, news and finally to any field with its own codes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一粒种子长出：认识字母变成读写能力，再变成可统计的数字，随后成为一套实用能力，扩展到屏幕、金钱、新闻，最后延伸到任何有自身规则的专业领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short pencil pressed on a page beside a signed form.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支削短的铅笔压在纸页上，旁边是一份签过名的表格。

branches.en: THE SEED: knowing letters is the oldest and simplest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 种子：认识字母是这个词最古老也最简单的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED: a state can turn the ability into a percentage, and the word follows.
branches.cn: 被计数：国家能把能力换算成百分比，词义也随之跟进。

branches.en: USING IT: forms and instructions on one side, a discipline's vocabulary on the other.
branches.cn: 会用：一边是表格与说明，另一边是某学科的专业词汇。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: screens and headlines each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新媒介：屏幕与标题各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: CODES OF THE WORLD: money and shared culture are also systems one must learn to read.
branches.cn: 世界的密码：金钱与共同文化同样是必须学会读懂的体系。

intro.en: The word is a short English noun built on a Latin root for a letter, with a suffix of state or quality.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的英语名词，建在拉丁语表「字母」的词根上，并带一个表状态或性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, letters and literature in English, while litteratus gives literate and, with a negating prefix, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 在英语里衍生出「字母」「书信」与「文学」，litteratus 则衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀又有「不识字的」。

items.meaning: a letter; writings in the plural
items.meaningCN: 字母；复数指书信或著作
items.example: The root names the smallest unit of written language.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指书面语言的最小单位。

items.meaning: a written sign for a speech sound
items.example: A single letter can change a whole meaning.
items.exampleCN: 一个字母就能改变整个意思。

items.example: The village is almost wholly literate now.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子如今几乎人人识字。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy was made a national target.
The forms were useless to illiterate tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些表格对不识字的租户毫无用处。

items.example: She read the literature on soil erosion.
items.exampleCN: 她读了关于土壤侵蚀的文献。

items.example: A literal translation missed the joke.
He was a man of letters in the old sense.
items.exampleCN: 在旧时的意义上，他是个文人。

definition_zh: 依照，按照（规定、法律、指示）；与……一致
definition_en: following or agreeing with a rule, law, instruction or standard
core_image: 一只手把申请表压在法条汇编上，逐条核对后盖章
scene: 审批员把申请表摊在法规汇编旁，逐条核对后盖章。 The permit was issued in accordance with the safety code.
sceneCN: 这里取「依照规定」（第 1 个义项：后接法规、规范等正式依据）；句意为许可证是依照安全规范签发的。

pos.zh: 介词短语：依照、按照（正式）
介词短语：与……一致、相符

forms.label: 正式变体
forms.form: in accordance with the provisions of

forms.label: 后置用法
forms.form: shall be conducted in accordance with

derivatives.zh: 根据（较口语的对应说法）

senses.title: Compliance with a law or regulation
senses.definition: used before the name of a law or regulation to say that an act follows it
senses.definitionCN: 用在法律或法规名称之前，表示行为遵循该规定
senses.example: The permit was issued in accordance with the safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证是依照安全规范签发的。
senses.why: The phrase turns a rule into the authority behind an act, which is why statutes are its most natural object.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把规则变成行为背后的授权依据，所以法规是它最自然的宾语。

senses.title: Acting on an instruction or authorization
senses.definition: used before an instruction or an authority to show that the action was authorized
senses.definitionCN: 用在指示或授权之前，表明行为获得许可
senses.example: Payment was released in accordance with your written instruction.
senses.exampleCN: 款项是依照你的书面指示放出的。
senses.why: With an instruction, the phrase answers the question of who authorized the act, not merely what rule exists.
senses.whyCN: 接指示时，这个短语回答「谁授权了这个动作」，而不只是说明有何规则。

senses.title: Agreement with facts or records
senses.definition: used before a statement of fact to say that a description matches the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用在事实陈述之前，表示描述与证据一致
senses.example: The report was corrected in accordance with the original records.
senses.exampleCN: 报告已依照原始记录作了更正。
senses.why: Here the phrase moves from obedience to correspondence: what is checked is accuracy, not permission.
senses.whyCN: 此处短语从「服从」转向「相符」：被检验的是准确，而非许可。

senses.title: Compliance with contract terms
senses.definition: used in contracts to bind a party to the terms already agreed
senses.definitionCN: 在合同中使用，使一方受已达成的条款约束
senses.example: The goods were delivered in accordance with clause four.
senses.exampleCN: 货物是依照第四条交付的。
senses.why: Contract drafting needs a phrase that points to the document itself as the standard, and this one does exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 合同起草需要一个以文件本身为准的说法，这个短语正好如此。

senses.title: Conformity with a technical standard
senses.definition: used before a standard or specification to state that a product or process meets it
senses.definitionCN: 用在标准或规格之前，说明产品或流程达到该要求
senses.example: The samples were tested in accordance with the national standard.
senses.exampleCN: 样品是依照国家标准检测的。
senses.why: In technical writing the phrase links a procedure to a published standard, so the method can be audited.
senses.whyCN: 在技术写作中，这个短语把流程挂到已公布的标准上，方法因而可被审核。

senses.title: The formal alternative to a plain phrase
senses.titleCN: 正式语域：书面替代口语说法
senses.definition: in official and academic prose it replaces the plainer phrase according to
senses.definitionCN: 在官方与学术文字中替代更口语的说法
senses.example: The forms must be filed in accordance with the guidance issued last year.
senses.exampleCN: 表格必须依照去年发布的指引提交。
senses.why: The phrase is chosen precisely because it sounds institutional; the everyday alternative would lower the register.
senses.whyCN: 选用这个短语正因为它听起来像机构语言；日常说法会把语域拉低。

senses.title: The routine formula in procedure documents
senses.definition: in manuals and procedure documents it frames an obligatory step in a fixed formula
senses.definitionCN: 在手册与程序文件中，以固定句式框定一个必须执行的步骤
senses.example: All inspections shall be conducted in accordance with the attached schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 所有检查均须依照所附日程进行。
senses.why: Procedure writing pairs shall with the phrase so that the obligation and its standard appear in one clause.
senses.whyCN: 程序写作把「须」与这个短语配对，使义务与标准出现在同一从句里。

senses.title: Consistency with a principle or intention
senses.definition: used before a principle or intention to say that an act expresses it consistently
senses.definitionCN: 用在原则或意愿之前，表示行为一贯地体现它
senses.example: The decision was made in accordance with the values the committee had stated.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定与委员会先前申明的价值取向一致。
senses.why: When the object is abstract, the phrase checks coherence over time rather than compliance with a written rule.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是抽象原则时，这个短语检验的是长期一致性，而非对成文规则的服从。

intro.en: Accordance comes from accord, which English took from Old French acorder, from Vulgar Latin accordare, from Latin ad, to, and cor, heart. The heart etymon is certain; the Vulgar Latin verb is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: accordance 来自 accord，英语经古法语 acorder 借入，其源头是通俗拉丁语 accordare，由拉丁语 ad「向」与 cor「心」构成。「心」这一词根确定；通俗拉丁语动词属重构形式。

items.en: Cor, cordis, heart, is also the source of cordial and record; to bring hearts together was to agree.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，也是 cordial 与 record 的来源；把心放到一起就是达成一致。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meant to reconcile or bring into harmony.
items.cn: 重构的动词意为调和、使和谐。

items.en: Old French acorder meant to be of one heart, and gave English the noun accord.
items.cn: 古法语 acorder 意为同心，给英语带来名词 accord。

items.en: Accordance, meaning agreement, is recorded in Middle English; the date is approximate.
items.cn: accordance 意为一致，见于中古英语，年代为约数。

items.en: The phrase with this preposition settles in modern legal and administrative writing.
items.cn: 带这个介词的短语在近代法律与行政文字中定型。

note.en: The first group marks a standard being followed but differs in formality or in what is followed; the second group holds formal ways of citing a rule.
note.cn: 第一组都标出所遵循的标准，但正式程度或所循对象不同；第二组是引用规则的正式说法。

entries.definition: It reports a source or a rule in neutral prose and can also mean as stated by.
entries.definitionCN: 它在中性文字中交代来源或规则，也可表「据……所说」。

entries.definition: It stresses harmony between parties rather than compliance with a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调各方和谐，而非对规则的遵守。

entries.definition: It is the regulator's phrase and foregrounds obedience to a requirement.
entries.definitionCN: 这是监管者的用语，突出对要求的服从。

entries.definition: Under plus a law is a shorter legal formula with the same authority.
entries.definitionCN: 「根据」加法律是更短的法律套语，授权意味相同。

entries.definition: A dense legal phrase meaning in carrying out the terms of.
entries.definitionCN: 一个密集的法律短语，意为「依……条款执行」。

entries.definition: It checks that two statements or acts do not contradict each other.
entries.definitionCN: 它检查两项陈述或行为是否互相矛盾。

entries.definition: It is the policy writer's phrase for keeping to an agreed direction.
entries.definitionCN: 政策写作者的用语，指与既定方向保持一致。

entries.definition: A brief business formula meaning according to, often criticized as informal.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的商务套语，意为「按照」，常被指为不够正式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real heart root, the real legal phrase and the real register.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的「心」词根、真实法律短语与真实语域。

normal.en: The root is heart: agreement was first a coming together of hearts.
normal.cn: 词根是「心」：一致最初指心走到一起。

normal.en: It takes a noun, never a clause; a whole statement needs the fact that frame.
normal.cn: 它接名词，从不接从句；完整命题要靠「事实是」框架。

normal.en: The object is usually a law, a rule, a standard or an instruction.
normal.cn: 宾语通常是法律、规则、标准或指示。

normal.en: Its everyday cousin according to is shorter and less institutional.
normal.cn: 它的日常表亲更短，也没那么机构化。

normal.en: In contracts it points to the document itself as the authority.
normal.cn: 在合同里，它把文件本身指为授权来源。

abstract.en: Like a stamp pressed onto a form only after the rule book has been checked line by line.
abstract.cn: 像逐条核对规则汇编之后，才在表格上盖章。

abstract.en: Like a road that follows the fence rather than cutting across it.
abstract.cn: 像一条顺着栅栏走、而不横穿过去的道路。

abstract.en: Like two hearts beating to the same rhythm before a signature is given.
abstract.cn: 像签字之前，两颗心按同一节奏跳动。

examples.en: The work was carried out in accordance with the agreed schedule.
examples.cn: 工作依照商定的日程进行。

examples.en: In accordance with the regulations, all visitors must register.
examples.cn: 依照规定，所有访客必须登记。

examples.en: The account was adjusted in accordance with the auditor's findings.
examples.cn: 账目已依照审计发现作了调整。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by the object followed: a law, an instruction, the facts, a contract clause, a technical standard, formal register, procedure formulas, and an abstract principle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按所循对象区分：法律、指示、事实、合同条款、技术标准、正式语域、公文句式、抽象原则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed only after the rule book has been checked line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐条核对规则汇编后才落下的印章。

branches.en: THE RULE: statutes and technical standards supply the authority for an act.
branches.cn: 规则：法规与技术标准为行为提供依据。

branches.en: THE AUTHORIZATION: instructions and contract clauses bind the act to a document.
branches.cn: 授权：指示与合同条款把行为绑到文件上。

branches.en: THE RECORD: accuracy is checked against the evidence rather than permission.
branches.cn: 记录：对照证据检验准确，而非许可。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: official prose and procedure formulas keep the phrase institutional.
branches.cn: 语域：官方文字与程序句式让它保持机构语气。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: an abstract value is checked for coherence over time.
branches.cn: 原则：抽象价值被检验是否长期一贯。

intro.en: The phrase joins a noun built on the Latin word for heart with an English preposition; the Latin core is transparent.
intro.cn: 这个短语把建在拉丁语「心」上的名词与英语介词结合；拉丁核心透明。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etymon is cor, heart, through the reconstructed Vulgar Latin verb accordare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 cor「心」，经通俗拉丁语重构动词 accordare 而来。

items.example: The root also gives cordial and record.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也给出另外两个英语词。

items.meaning: to reconcile; to bring into harmony
items.example: The verb is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词属重构，并非有直接记录。

items.meaning: to agree; to be of one heart
items.example: French passed the verb and its noun to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个动词及其名词传给英语。

items.example: The noun still means a mutual agreement.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词至今指相互一致。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成表状态的名词。

items.example: The participle heads the everyday phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词领起日常说法。

items.example: The adverb marks a consequence or a fit.
The phrase is standard in statutes and manuals.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语在法规与手册中是标准用法。

definition_zh: 与……形成鲜明对照；与……截然相反，用来突出两者的对立或差别
definition_en: used to introduce a thing that differs sharply from the one just mentioned or from what would be expected
core_image: 同一张展台上左边满杯、右边空杯，两束灯光的颜色正好相反
scene: 展台两侧并排放着满杯与空杯，标签特意标出两者的差别。 In contrast to the first case, the second case held an empty cup.
sceneCN: 这里指第二个展柜与第一个恰好相反（第 1 个义项：与……形成鲜明对照）；句意为与第一个展柜不同，第二个展柜里是空杯。图中可辨识物件：展台、满杯、空杯、两束灯光。

pos.zh: 介词短语：与……形成对照
状语短语：相比之下

collocations.phrase: in contrast to the situation elsewhere

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「对立而站」一系经意大利语、法语而来，义为「对照；形成对比」
由该名词加「有……性质」的形容词尾构成，义为「对比的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「对比之下」
由介词加名词构成的独立连接语，义为「相比之下」
由动词加介词构成，义为「与……形成对比」

senses.title: A sharp opposition
senses.definition: used to set a thing against another that is sharply different
senses.definitionCN: 把一物与另一明显不同之物并置
senses.example: In contrast to the coastal towns, the inland villages lost population.
senses.exampleCN: 与沿海城镇相反，内陆村庄人口减少。
senses.why: The preposition names the second term, and the sentence asserts a difference rather than a shared measure.
senses.whyCN: 介词点出第二项，句子断言的是差异而不是共同的尺度。

senses.title: The fronted frame
senses.definition: placed at the front of a clause to announce that the opposite case follows
senses.definitionCN: 置于从句开头，宣告接下来是相反的情形
senses.example: In contrast to the north, the south relies on service industries.
senses.exampleCN: 与北方相反，南方依靠服务业。
senses.why: Fronting makes the contrast structural: the reader knows the second half will mirror, then reverse, the first.
senses.whyCN: 前置让对照成为结构性的：读者知道后半句先对应、后反转前半句。

senses.title: Against expectation
senses.titleCN: 与预期或普遍看法相反
senses.definition: used to correct an assumption that the reader is likely to hold
senses.definitionCN: 用来纠正读者可能持有的假设
senses.example: In contrast to popular belief, the desert supports a rich microbial life.
senses.exampleCN: 与普遍看法相反，沙漠里生活着丰富的微生物。
senses.why: Here the first term is not a fact but a belief, so the phrase does the work of a correction.
senses.whyCN: 这里的第一项不是事实而是看法，短语因此承担纠正的功能。

senses.title: Against the evidence
senses.definition: used in research writing to introduce a result that opposes an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中引出与先前结果相反的结果
senses.example: In contrast to the earlier trial, the second trial found no benefit.
senses.exampleCN: 与早先的试验相反，第二次试验没有发现益处。
senses.why: Research prose needs to mark disagreement without calling the earlier work wrong, and this frame does exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作需要标出分歧又不判定早先工作错误，这一框架正好做到。

senses.title: A difference in kind
senses.definition: used when two things differ in nature rather than in degree
senses.definitionCN: 两者在性质上不同，而非程度不同
senses.example: In contrast to a loan, a grant never has to be repaid.
senses.exampleCN: 与贷款不同，赠款从不需要偿还。
senses.why: When the difference is categorical, contrast is the right tool and comparison would understate it.
senses.whyCN: 差异是类别性的时候，对照才合适，比较会低估它。

senses.title: Syntactic division of labour
senses.definition: used with a following noun, where by contrast would stand alone
senses.definitionCN: 后面接名词，而独立连接语则单独使用
senses.example: In contrast to the first group, the second group met every target.
senses.exampleCN: 与第一组相反，第二组达成了全部目标。
senses.why: The two forms split the work: this one takes a benchmark, while by contrast takes none.
senses.whyCN: 两种形式分工：这一个带基准，另一个不带。

senses.title: Graded sharpness
senses.definition: used with sharp or marked to raise the force of the difference
senses.definitionCN: 与「鲜明的」「显著的」一类词连用以提高差异的力度
senses.example: In contrast to last year, sales fell in every region, a sharp reversal.
senses.exampleCN: 与去年相反，各地销量都下降了，形成鲜明反转。
senses.why: The modifier sits inside the phrase, so force is added without changing the frame.
senses.whyCN: 修饰语插在短语内部，力度增强而框架不变。

senses.title: Parallel-structure contrast
senses.definition: used to balance two opposite statements in one sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在同一句中平衡两个相反的陈述
senses.example: In contrast to the north, where prices rose, the south saw prices fall.
senses.exampleCN: 与物价上涨的北方相反，南方物价下跌。
senses.why: Parallel wording makes the reversal measurable; the phrase marks where the second half begins.
senses.whyCN: 平行措辞让反转可衡量，短语标出后半句的起点。

intro.en: Contrast came into English through French from Italian contrastare, a verb reconstructed in Vulgar Latin from Latin contra, against, and stare, to stand. The reconstruction is reliable; the date of the English phrase is approximate.
intro.cn: contrast 经法语、意大利语进入英语，其动词是通俗拉丁语中由 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」构成的重构形式。该重构可靠；英语短语的年代为约数。

items.en: Contra means against and appears in contradiction and contraflow.
items.cn: contra 意为「反对」，也出现在 contradiction 与 contraflow 中。

items.en: Stare means to stand, giving the picture of two things standing face to face.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立」，画出两物面对面站立的画面。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meant to stand against or withstand.
items.cn: 重构动词意为「对立而站、抵抗」。

items.en: Italian contrastare passed into French as contraster and then into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 意大利语 contrastare 传入法语作 contraster，十六世纪再进入英语。

items.en: The prepositional frame belongs to modern written English; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 这一介词框架属近代书面英语，确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the contrast slot with different prepositions or functions; the second group holds other ways of marking opposition.
note.cn: 第一组占同一对照位置，但介词或功能不同；第二组是其他标记对立的方式。

entries.definition: With is the older and more bookish partner of to, with the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: with 是 to 更旧、更书面的搭档，意义相同。

entries.definition: It weighs two items on one scale rather than declaring them opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两项放在同一尺度上称量，而非宣告对立。

entries.definition: It works alone between clauses and takes no noun after it.
entries.definitionCN: 它独立用于句间，后面不接名词。

entries.definition: It rejects a stated negative claim; contrast merely sets two facts side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 它否定被说出的否定命题；对照只把两件事并置。

entries.definition: It simply names the different item, with no signal of rhetorical weight.
entries.definitionCN: 它只点出不同之物，不带修辞力度的信号。

entries.definition: It joins two full clauses that differ, common in formal and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 它连接两个不同的完整从句，多见于正式与法律文本。

entries.definition: It separates two options and usually implies a preference.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两个选项分开，通常暗示偏好。

entries.definition: It marks the reverse side of a relation rather than a plain difference.
entries.definitionCN: 它标出关系的反面，而非单纯差异。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real Latin pair, the real prepositions and the contrast-comparison split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁语对、真实介词以及对照与比较的分工。

normal.en: Contra is against and stare is to stand, so the two things stand face to face.
normal.cn: 词根一是「反」、一是「站」，两物便面对面站着。

normal.en: To takes a noun; by contrast stands alone.
normal.cn: 带介词的形式接名词，独立形式单独使用。

normal.en: At the front it announces the other side; mid-sentence it pivots.
normal.cn: 句首宣告另一面，句中完成转折。

normal.en: Sharp and marked go inside the phrase to raise the force.
normal.cn: 表示「鲜明」「显著」的词插在短语内部增强力度。

normal.en: Contrast opposes; comparison weighs. Mixing them weakens both.
normal.cn: 对照管对立，比较管称量，混用会削弱两者。

abstract.en: Like two lamps of opposite colours lit at the two ends of one table.
abstract.cn: 像同一张桌子两端亮起两盏颜色相反的灯。

abstract.en: Like a hinge in the middle of a sentence, letting the second half swing the other way.
abstract.cn: 像句子中间的一枚铰链，让后半句向另一边转。

abstract.en: Like a scale with one full pan and one empty pan, both visible at once.
abstract.cn: 像一架天平，一端满一端空，同时可见。

examples.en: In contrast to the earlier model, the new model runs on a single battery.
examples.cn: 与早先的型号相反，新机型只靠一节电池运行。

examples.en: In contrast to the coastal group, the inland group moved less.
examples.cn: 与沿海组相反，内陆组流动更少。

examples.en: In contrast to last winter, this winter has been mild.
examples.cn: 与去年冬天相反，今年冬天一直温和。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by what is being opposed: another fact, a fronted opposite case, an expectation, earlier evidence, a different kind, a syntactic partner, a graded difference and a parallel clause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按对立对象区分：另一事实、前置相反情形、预期、早先证据、不同类别、句法搭档、分级差异、平行从句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one full cup and one empty cup under two lights of opposite colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：满杯与空杯摆在两束相反颜色的灯光下。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: the second clause mirrors the first and then reverses it.
branches.cn: 镜像：后半句先对应前半句，再反转。

branches.en: THE CORRECTION: the first term is a belief, so the phrase sets the record straight.
branches.cn: 纠正：第一项是看法，短语借此澄清事实。

branches.en: THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE: research uses it to mark disagreement without blame.
branches.cn: 反证：研究用它标出分歧而不追责。

branches.en: THE CATEGORICAL GAP: two kinds or two parallel clauses are set apart.
branches.cn: 类别落差：两个类别或两个平行从句被分开。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND ITS FORCE: a following noun, plus sharp or marked inside.
branches.cn: 框架与力度：后接名词，内部可加「鲜明」「显著」。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin preposition of opposition to a Latin verb of standing; the verb reached English through Italian and French.
intro.cn: 短语把表对立的拉丁介词与表站立的拉丁动词结合起来；动词经意大利语、法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are contra, against, and stare, to stand; contrastare is the reconstructed Vulgar Latin link.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」；contrastare 是通俗拉丁语的重构环节。

items.example: Contra appears in many English compounds of opposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词出现在许多表对立的英语复合词里。

items.example: The verb supplies the image of standing one's ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「站定不退」的画面。

items.example: The reconstructed verb links Latin to Italian.
items.exampleCN: 重构动词把拉丁语与意大利语接上。

items.example: French carried the verb into English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 法语在十六世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: The noun names the difference that the phrase points to.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名短语所指出的差异。

items.example: Linguistics speaks of contrastive pairs.

items.exampleCN: 这个短语以名词作基准。

items.example: Its twin usually stands alone between sentences.

senses.title: A burrowing shellfish
senses.definition: a soft-bodied shellfish with a hinged shell that lives in sand
senses.definitionCN: 带铰合壳、生活在沙中的软体贝类
senses.example: We gathered clams at the water edge.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在水边捡蛤蜊。

senses.title: To refuse to speak
senses.definition: informal, to stay silent and give nothing away
senses.definitionCN: 口语，保持沉默，什么也不透露
senses.example: He clammed up when the police arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 警察一到，他就闭口不言了。
senses.why: The shut shell became a picture of a closed mouth.
senses.whyCN: 紧闭的壳成了闭嘴的形象。

intro.cn: clam 最初指抓握、束缚，后指紧紧合壳的贝类。

items.en: Clam means a bond or grip.
items.cn: 古英语 clam 意为束缚、抓握。

items.en: The word names a shell that clamps shut.
items.cn: 十六世纪用它指紧紧合壳的贝类。

items.en: Clam chowder spreads with American cooking.
items.cn: 十九世纪蛤蜊浓汤随美国烹饪传播。

items.en: The idiom clammed up means to fall silent.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现 clammed up 的沉默义。

items.en: The food sense and the idiom both survive.
items.cn: 现代的食用义与习语义都保留着。

note.cn: 形近组与 clam 只差一个字母；近义组列出其他贝类。

entries.definition: A dark shellfish in a long shell.

definition_zh: 幼苗；由种子长成的小苗
definition_en: a very young plant that has grown from a seed and is not yet mature
core_image: 育苗盘里一株小小的番茄苗，两片圆圆的子叶顶在细茎上
scene: 温室里，育苗盘排成几行，刚出土的番茄只有两片圆叶。 Each seedling in the tray has two seed leaves and a thread-like root.
sceneCN: 这里 seedling 指「幼苗」（第 1 个义项：由种子长出的幼小植株）；句意为托盘里每一株幼苗都有两片子叶和一根线一样的根。

pos.zh: 幼苗；实生苗；小苗

senses.title: A young plant from a seed
senses.titleCN: 由种子长出的幼小植株
senses.definition: a plant that has recently grown from a seed and has only a few leaves
senses.definitionCN: 刚从种子长出、只有几片叶子的植物
senses.example: Each seedling was labelled with its parent line.
senses.exampleCN: 每株幼苗都标着亲本编号。
senses.why: seed plus the diminutive -ling makes 'a little seed-thing', which is exactly what the noun names.
senses.whyCN: seed 加指小后缀 -ling 构成「小小的种子之物」，正是这个名词所指。

senses.title: The seedling stage of growth
senses.definition: the growth stage between sprouting and the appearance of mature leaves
senses.definitionCN: 从发芽到长出成熟叶之间的生长阶段
senses.example: The plants are most vulnerable at the seedling stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物在幼苗期最为脆弱。
senses.why: the noun can name a stage because young plants are defined by being at that age.
senses.whyCN: 名词可以命名一个阶段，因为幼小植株正是以「处于这个年龄」来定义的。

senses.title: A plant ready to be transplanted
senses.definition: a young plant raised in a tray or bed and then moved to the field
senses.definitionCN: 在托盘或苗床育成、随后移入田间的幼株
senses.example: The seedlings were hardened off before transplanting.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗在移栽前经过了炼苗。
senses.why: nursery practice turns the age word into a handling category, meaning the plant is old enough to move.
senses.whyCN: 苗圃实践把这个年龄词变成操作类别，意为植株已大到可以搬动。

senses.title: A young tree
senses.definition: a tree grown from seed and still small enough to be lifted
senses.definitionCN: 由种子长成、仍小到可以起苗的树
senses.example: Two thousand tree seedlings went into the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 两千株树苗被种进山坡。
senses.why: the same noun works for woody plants because the age, not the habit, is what it measures.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词适用于木本植物，因为它量的是年龄，而不是生长习性。

senses.title: A measure of early vigour
senses.titleCN: 幼苗活力（作为质量指标）
senses.definition: the quality of early growth, judged by size, colour and root development
senses.definitionCN: 早期生长的质量，以大小、颜色与根系发育衡量
senses.example: Seedling vigour predicted how many would survive the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗活力预示了有多少能越冬存活。
senses.why: the noun becomes a quality index because the first weeks decide the rest of the season.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成质量指标，因为最初几周决定了整个季节。

senses.title: A plant living in a nursery bed
senses.definition: a plant raised densely in a bed or tray before being spaced out
senses.definitionCN: 在苗床或托盘中密集育成、之后才分开的植株
senses.example: The seedling bed was covered with fleece for the cold nights.
senses.exampleCN: 苗床在寒夜里盖上了保温布。
senses.why: the noun attaches to the plant, and the place is named by compounding it with bed.
senses.whyCN: 名词附着于植株，地点则通过与「床」复合来命名。

senses.title: A plant that survives establishment
senses.definition: a young plant that has taken root in its final position
senses.definitionCN: 在最终位置扎根成活的幼株
senses.example: Seedling establishment failed on the exposed slope.
senses.exampleCN: 在裸露的坡面上幼苗定植失败。
senses.why: establishment is germination's second test, so the noun marks the plant that has passed both.
senses.whyCN: 定植是萌发之后的第二道考验，名词因此标记通过了这两关的植株。

senses.title: Metaphor: an early-stage venture
senses.titleCN: 比喻：处于初期的事业或项目
senses.definition: figurative, an organisation or project in its first fragile period
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，处于最初脆弱阶段的机构或项目
senses.example: The grant was meant for seedlings, not for established firms.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助是给初创者的，而不是给成熟企业的。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps fragility and small size, and drops the soil.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留脆弱与幼小，舍去土壤。

intro.en: Seedling is an English compound of seed, from Old English sæd, and the diminutive suffix -ling 'one belonging to or young'. It has no Latin ancestor of its own. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: seedling 是英语复合词，由古英语 sæd「种子」与指小后缀 -ling「属于……的、年幼的」构成，本身没有拉丁语来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sæd meant 'seed' and descends from Proto-Germanic *sediz; the verb sow and the noun seed split early in English.
items.cn: sæd 意为「种子」，源自原始日耳曼语 *sediz；动词 sow 与名词 seed 在英语中很早就分开了。

items.en: The suffix -ling marks a person or animal belonging to a class, or a young one, as in duckling and yearling.
items.cn: 后缀 -ling 标记属于某类的幼小者，如 duckling 与 yearling。

items.en: Seedling therefore reads as 'a young thing of the seed kind', i.e. a plant raised from seed rather than from a cutting.
items.cn: 因此 seedling 读作「种子一类的幼小者」，即由种子而非插条育成的植株。

items.en: The word became standard in forestry and horticulture once nurseries separated seed-raised from cutting-raised stock.
items.cn: 当苗圃把实生苗与扦插苗分开之后，这个词在林业与园艺中成为标准用语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest recorded use of seedling is not firmly dated here; the -ling suffix has been productive since Old English.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：seedling 最早的书证年代在此未能确证；-ling 后缀自上古英语起一直能产。

note.en: Group one separates the -ling words that look alike; group two separates a seed-raised plant from plants raised other ways or at other stages.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近的 -ling 词；第二组区分实生苗与其他繁殖方式或阶段的植株。

entries.definition: The reproductive unit itself; a seedling is what it becomes after germination.
entries.definitionCN: 繁殖单位本身；幼苗是它萌发之后变成的样子。

entries.definition: The act of sowing, or the young crop as a mass; it names the operation or the whole stand, not one plant.
entries.definitionCN: 播种这一动作，或作为整体的幼苗；命名操作或整片植株，而非单株。

entries.definition: A young duck, built exactly like seedling from base plus -ling; the pattern is shared but the meaning is not.
entries.definitionCN: 小鸭，构词方式与 seedling 完全相同；模式相同而词义无关。

entries.definition: An animal one year old, formed with -ling; it shows the suffix measures age, which is why seedling works for stage two.
entries.definitionCN: 一岁的动物，由 -ling 构成；说明这个后缀量的是年龄，这也是 seedling 能指幼苗阶段的原因。

entries.definition: A young tree, especially one with a slender trunk; it is narrower than seedling, which can be any young plant.
entries.definitionCN: 幼树，尤指树干细长者；比 seedling 窄，后者可指任何幼小植株。

entries.definition: A shoot growing from a seed or root, often eaten as a vegetable; a seedling is the whole young plant.
entries.definitionCN: 从种子或根长出的新芽，常作蔬菜食用；幼苗则是整株幼小植物。

entries.definition: A piece of stem or leaf rooted to make a new plant; a seedling by definition comes from a seed.
entries.definitionCN: 一段茎或叶生根形成新株；幼苗按定义来自种子。

entries.definition: The act of moving a young plant to its final place; the plant before the move is the seedling.
entries.definitionCN: 把幼株移到最终位置的动作；移动之前的植株就是幼苗。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real compound, the real nursery phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合构词、真实的苗圃搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: seed + -ling: a little seed-thing, now a plant.
normal.cn: seed + -ling：小小的种子之物，如今成了一株植物。

normal.en: The same suffix gives duckling and yearling, all young things.
normal.cn: 同一后缀构成 duckling 与 yearling，都是幼小者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seedling stage, seedling vigour, transplant seedlings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：幼苗期、幼苗活力、移栽幼苗。

normal.en: The tray is the first home; the field is the second.
normal.cn: 育苗盘是第一个家，田间是第二个。

normal.en: The family runs seed, seedbed, seeding, seedling, seedless.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 seed、seedbed、seeding、seedling、seedless。

abstract.en: Picture a fragile green thing the size of a finger, standing in a vast bare field.
abstract.cn: 想象一株手指大小的脆弱绿苗，站在空旷的大田里。

abstract.en: Picture a new firm with three people and one borrowed desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一家新公司，三个人，一张借来的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a small idea that has roots but no height yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小想法，已生根，却还没有高度。

examples.en: The seedlings were ready to go out after three weeks.
examples.cn: 三周后这些幼苗可以出圃了。

examples.en: Seedling vigour depends on the quality of the seed lot.
examples.cn: 幼苗活力取决于种子批次的质量。

examples.en: Deer browsed every seedling on the lower slope.
examples.cn: 鹿把低坡上的幼苗全都啃了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seed（种子）+ ling（小的）」——种子变成的小东西 → 幼苗

root: 古英语 sæd「种子」（原始日耳曼语 *sediz）+ 指小后缀 -ling；英语本族复合词，无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of seedling follow one small plant from the tray to the field, from a stage to a measure of vigour, and finally to any young enterprise.
sensesIntro.cn: seedling 的八个义项跟着一株小苗从托盘走到田间，从阶段变成活力指标，最后延伸到任何初创的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger-sized green thing standing in a tray of soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株手指大小的绿色小苗立在土盘里。

branches.en: THE PLANT AND ITS AGE: one noun covers the individual and the stage it is in.
branches.cn: 植株与年龄：一个名词同时覆盖个体与它所处的阶段。

branches.en: NURSERY LIFE: raised in a bed, moved out, and finally rooted in place.
branches.cn: 苗圃生涯：在苗床育成、移出、最终在原地扎根。

branches.en: WOODY CASE: the same word serves a young tree.
branches.cn: 木本情形：同一个词也用于幼树。

branches.en: MEASURED QUALITY: early growth becomes a number for growers.
branches.cn: 可量的质量：早期生长成为种植者的指标。

branches.en: METAPHOR: a new venture is small, rooted and fragile.
branches.cn: 比喻：新事业同样幼小、有根而脆弱。

intro.en: Seedling is a native English compound, so its parts are an old noun and an old suffix rather than Latin morphemes.
intro.cn: seedling 是英语本族复合词，其成分是古老的名词与古老的后缀，而非拉丁语素。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: seed descends from Old English sæd and -ling is a Germanic diminutive suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 没有适用的拉丁词条：seed 源自上古英语 sæd，-ling 是日耳曼语指小后缀。
