items.example: They transplant the seedlings in May.

definition_zh: 民族国家；指疆界与民族共同体大致重合、以民族认同整合的主权国家
definition_en: a sovereign state whose territory is understood to coincide with the homeland of one people
core_image: 两张透明地图叠在灯下，一张画国界，一张画方言分布，两条线几乎重合
scene: 会议室的墙上并排挂着两张地图，一张画国界，一张画方言分布，讲解的人用两支笔同时描过两条线。 The nation-state rests on the hope that a border and a language map can be made to coincide.
sceneCN: 这里 nation-state 指「疆界与民族分布大致重合的国家形态」（第 1 个义项：以民族共同体为其领土基础的主权国家）；句意为民族国家建立在这样一个希望上：国界与语言地图能够被画成同一条线。图中可辨识物件：两张地图、两支描线笔、投影灯、会议桌。

pos.zh: 民族国家（可数，复数 nation-states；亦作定语，如 nation-state system）

derivatives.zh: 民族（拉丁 natio「同出一源的人群」，出自 nasci「出生」）
民族主义（national 加 -ism，指以民族为中心的主张）
国家；状态（拉丁 status「站立的状态」，出自 stare「站立」）
国家地位（state 加 -hood，指成为国家的状态）
无国籍的；无国家的（state 加 -less，指不属任何国家）
民族地位；民族意识（nation 加 -hood，指成为民族的状态）

senses.title: A state whose borders match a people
senses.titleCN: 疆界与民族大致重合的国家
senses.definition: a state that claims to be the political home of one people, with borders treated as the edge of that homeland
senses.definitionCN: 声称是某一民族政治家园的国家，其边界被视为该民族家园的边缘
senses.example: The nation-state rests on the hope that a border and a language map can be made to coincide.
senses.exampleCN: 民族国家建立在这样一个希望上：国界与语言地图能够被画成同一条线。
senses.why: The compound simply puts the two nouns side by side, so its core sense is the fit between a people and a state.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是把两个名词并排，因此核心意思就是「民族与国家相合」。

senses.title: The ideal type in political science
senses.definition: a model used for comparison rather than a description of any real country, since most states contain several peoples
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较的模型，而非对任何现实国家的描述，因为多数国家内部都有多个民族
senses.example: Analysts treat the nation-state as an ideal type, not a census category.
senses.exampleCN: 分析者把民族国家当作理想类型，而不是人口统计类别。
senses.why: Once scholars need a benchmark to measure real states against, the word becomes a theoretical model rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 当学者需要一个基准来衡量现实国家，这个词就变成理论模型，而不再是一个地点。

senses.title: The historical product of nineteenth-century nationalism
senses.titleCN: 十九世纪民族主义的历史产物
senses.definition: the form of state that emerged in Europe when nationalist movements merged cultural nations with existing administrative units
senses.definitionCN: 欧洲民族主义运动把文化民族与既有行政单元合并后出现的国家形态
senses.example: The nation-state was assembled from provinces that had never shared a school system.
senses.exampleCN: 这个民族国家由从未共用过一套学校体系的多个省份拼合而成。
senses.why: The thing itself has a birthday: railways, schools and newspapers let a state standardize one language across its territory.
senses.whyCN: 这一事物本身有诞生日：铁路、学校与报纸让国家能在领土上标准化一种语言。

senses.title: An ethnic nation-state
senses.titleCN: 以族裔核心为基础的民族国家
senses.definition: a state that defines belonging by ancestry and treats one ethnic group's culture as the national culture
senses.definitionCN: 以祖源界定归属、并把某一族群的文化当作国家文化的国家
senses.example: An ethnic nation-state can make old minorities feel newly foreign.
senses.exampleCN: 以族裔为核心的民族国家会让原有少数群体突然觉得自己是外人。
senses.why: If the nation is a people born together, the most literal state is one whose institutions reproduce that birth group.
senses.whyCN: 如果民族是「同出一源的一群人」，最字面意义上的国家就是其制度复制这一血缘群体的国家。

senses.title: A civic nation-state
senses.titleCN: 以公民身份为基础的民族国家
senses.definition: a state that builds national unity from citizenship, law and shared political values rather than descent
senses.definitionCN: 以公民身份、法律与共同政治价值而非血统来建立国家团结的国家
senses.example: A civic nation-state can absorb newcomers through school and naturalization.
senses.exampleCN: 公民民族国家可以通过学校与入籍吸收新来者。
senses.why: The same compound supports a different answer to who belongs, since the people can be defined by law instead of blood.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合词也支持对「谁属于这里」的不同回答，因为人民可以由法律而非血统来界定。

senses.title: The nation-state as a sovereign actor
senses.titleCN: 作为主权行动者的民族国家
senses.definition: the unit treated as a single legal person in international relations, with borders, treaties and a seat at the table
senses.definitionCN: 在国际关系中被当作单一法律人格的单位，拥有边界、条约与谈判席位
senses.example: Global markets now move faster than the nation-state can legislate.
senses.exampleCN: 全球市场的变动速度已快过民族国家的立法速度。
senses.why: Because the state half supplies sovereignty, the compound also names the basic actor in diplomacy and international law.
senses.whyCN: 因为后半的 state 提供主权，这个复合词也命名外交与国际法中的基本行动者。

senses.title: The model pursued by postcolonial state-builders
senses.titleCN: 后殖民建国者追求的模型
senses.definition: the template adopted by new states that inherited colonial borders and tried to turn them into national homelands
senses.definitionCN: 继承殖民边界并试图把这些边界变成民族家园的新国家所采用的模板
senses.example: Postcolonial leaders inherited a nation-state whose borders cut through several peoples.
senses.exampleCN: 后殖民领导人继承了一个边界穿过数个民族的民族国家。
senses.why: Independence handed new governments colonial maps, and the compound names the ambition of turning those maps into nations.
senses.whyCN: 独立把殖民地图交给新政府，而这个复合词命名了把这些地图变成民族的雄心。

senses.title: The attributive use in debates about globalization
senses.titleCN: 讨论全球化时作定语的用法
senses.definition: used before nouns such as system, building or sovereignty to name the political order being defended or eroded
senses.definitionCN: 置于 system、building、sovereignty 等名词前，指正在被捍卫或被侵蚀的政治秩序
senses.example: The nation-state system is older than most of its members.
senses.exampleCN: 民族国家体系比它的大多数成员都要古老。
senses.why: When writers need a shorthand for the whole order, the compound works as a modifier without losing its two-part shape.
senses.whyCN: 当作者需要指称整个秩序的简称时，这个复合词就充当修饰语，而两部分的结构仍然保留。

intro.en: Nation-state is a modern compound of a Latin birth-noun and a Latin standing-noun, coined when the two ideas were deliberately fused. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nation-state 是把一个表示出生的拉丁名词与一个表示站立状态的拉丁名词组成的现代复合词，造出时正是要把这两个观念有意熔合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Natio meant 'birth, origin' and then 'a people of common birth', from nasci 'to be born'; its deeper root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: natio 意为「出生、出身」，继而指「同出一源的人群」，出自 nasci「出生」；更深词根属重构形式。

items.en: Status meant 'a standing, a condition', from stare 'to stand'; it named a person's legal position before it named a polity.
items.cn: status 意为「站立的状态、处境」，出自 stare「站立」；它先指个人的法律地位，后来才指政治共同体。

items.en: English state first meant a condition or a rank, and only in the sixteenth century came to mean the organized political community of a territory.
items.cn: 英语 state 最初指状态或等级，直到十六世纪才指一片领土上有组织的政治共同体。

items.en: The two words were joined in the early twentieth century to name a state that claims to be the home of one people, a term needed once empires broke into successor states.
items.cn: 这两个词在二十世纪初组合，用来指声称是一个民族家园的国家；帝国分裂为后继国家后，这一术语变得必要。

items.en: Mid-twentieth-century scholarship turned the compound into an ideal type, and it now names a model as often as a place.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期的学术研究把这个复合词变成理想类型，如今它既指地点，也同样常指模型。

items.en: Source uncertain (dates and reconstruction): the first written use of the hyphenated compound is dated differently by different reference works, and the pre-Latin roots of both halves are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（年代与重构）：这个带连字符的复合词最早的书面用例，各家工具书给出的年代不一；前后两半在拉丁语之前的词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the component words and near-identical compounds that get swapped; group two holds other political forms that are defined against it.
note.cn: 第一组是构成词与极易替换的近形复合词；第二组是与之相对照的其他政治形态。

entries.definition: The people alone; it says nothing about a state, which is why a nation can exist without one.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指人群，不涉及国家，因此民族可以没有国家。

entries.definition: The political and legal apparatus alone; a state may contain many nations or only part of one.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指政治法律机构；一个国家可以包含多个民族，也可以只含某一民族的一部分。

entries.definition: The condition of being a nation; it is a status, while the compound names an institutional form.
entries.definitionCN: 指成为民族的状态；它是身份，而这个复合词指制度形态。

entries.definition: The process of forging a shared national identity; the compound is the resulting structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指锻造共同民族身份的过程；复合词指由此形成的结构。

entries.definition: A state that openly contains several nations and does not claim to belong to one people.
entries.definitionCN: 公开包含多个民族、且不声称属于单一人群的国家。

entries.definition: The international-law term for an independent state, silent on whether its borders match a nation.
entries.definitionCN: 国际法中指独立国家的术语，不涉及边界是否与民族重合。

entries.definition: A sovereign city and its hinterland, a form older than the national model and organized around a town rather than a people.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有主权的城市及其腹地，这种形态早于民族模型，以城镇而非民族为中心。

entries.definition: A polity holding many nations under one sovereign; it is the historic opposite of the one-people ideal.
entries.definitionCN: 把多个民族置于一位君主之下的政体，是「一族一国」理想的历史对立面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Nation 'a people born together' plus state 'a standing political order': two halves, one claim that they fit.
normal.cn: nation「同出一源的人群」加 state「站立的政治秩序」：两半，一个「二者相合」的主张。

normal.en: The hyphen is doing work: it marks a fusion that is desired rather than a fact that is observed.
normal.cn: 连字符在起作用：它标记一种被期望的熔合，而非被观察到的事实。

normal.en: The family runs nation, national, nationalism, state, statehood, stateless, nationhood.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 nation、national、nationalism、state、statehood、stateless、nationhood。

normal.en: Fixed collocations mark the debates: nation-state system, nation-state building, the rise of the nation-state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出相关争论：民族国家体系、民族国家建构、民族国家的兴起。

normal.en: The contrasting term is multinational state, which exists because most real states hold several peoples.
normal.cn: 对照术语是多民族国家，它的存在正因为多数现实国家包含多个民族。

abstract.en: Picture two sheets of tracing paper laid one over the other until their lines almost touch.
abstract.cn: 想象两张描图纸叠在一起，直到它们的线条几乎贴合。

abstract.en: Picture a passport and a family tree printed on the same page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本护照与一棵家族树被印在同一页上。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom map where the colour of the language and the colour of the border are the same shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一张教室地图上，语言的颜色与边界的颜色是同一种色调。

examples.en: The peace conference tried to fit nation-states onto maps drawn for empires.
examples.cn: 和会试图把民族国家套进为帝国绘制的地图上。

examples.en: Migration has made the pure nation-state rare in practice.
examples.cn: 移民使纯粹的民族国家在现实中变得少见。

examples.en: The nation-state remains the unit that issues passports and signs treaties.
examples.cn: 民族国家仍是签发护照与签署条约的单位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nation（民族）+ state（国家）」——让民族的边界长成国家的边界 → 民族国家

root: nation 出自拉丁 natio「同出一源的人群」（nasci「出生」）；state 出自拉丁 status「站立的状态」（stare「站立」）。复合词把「人群」与「政治秩序」并置，主张二者边界重合，是近代民族主义兴起后的产物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one fit: a people is matched to a state, and the match is then used as an ideal type, a historical product, an ethnic model, a civic model, a sovereign actor, a postcolonial ambition, and a shorthand for the whole order.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「吻合」展开：人群与国家被配对，这一配对再被用作理想类型、历史产物、族裔模型、公民模型、主权行动者、后殖民雄心，以及整个秩序的简称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line laid directly on top of a language boundary until the two become one line.
core.cn: 核心意象：把国界线直接压在语言分界线上，直到两条线变成一条。

branches.en: FIT AND MODEL: the same match is both a claim about places and a benchmark for comparing them.
branches.cn: 吻合与模型：同一种配对既是对地方的断言，也是比较它们的基准。

branches.en: HISTORICAL BIRTH: schools, railways and newspapers made the fit possible in the nineteenth century.
branches.cn: 历史诞生：学校、铁路与报纸在十九世纪使这种吻合成为可能。

branches.en: TWO ANSWERS: descent and citizenship are rival definitions of the people being fitted to the state.
branches.cn: 两个答案：血统与公民身份是对「被配对的人群」的竞争性定义。

branches.en: SOVEREIGN ORDER: one actor at the table, and a whole system of such actors.
branches.cn: 主权秩序：谈判桌上的一个行动者，以及由这类行动者构成的整个体系。

branches.en: POSTCOLONIAL HOPE: inherited colonial lines are asked to become national homes.
branches.cn: 后殖民希望：继承来的殖民边界被要求变成民族家园。

intro.en: Both halves keep their own morphology: a birth-noun with its suffixes, and a standing-noun that also yields status words.
intro.cn: 前后两半都保留各自的构词：一个带后缀的出生名词，以及一个同样衍生状态类词的站立名词。

latinIntro.en: Nasci and natio build the first half; stare and status build the second, and English added -hood and -less to both.
latinIntro.cn: nasci 与 natio 构成前半，stare 与 status 构成后半，英语又给两半分别加上 -hood 与 -less。

items.example: The verb supplies the people's shared origin.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供人群的共同出身。

items.example: The noun supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的前半。

items.structure: stare, steti, statum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the image of something standing firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「稳固站立」的意象。

items.example: The noun moves from a person's rank to a polity's order.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从个人等级转到政治秩序的层面。

items.meaningCN: 状态；有组织的政治共同体
items.example: The second half supplies sovereignty.

items.meaning: a state claiming one people as its base
items.meaningCN: 以单一民族为基础的国家
items.example: The compound asserts a fit rather than describing one.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是主张一种吻合，而非描述一种吻合。

items.example: The suffix yields nationhood and statehood.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出 nationhood 与 statehood。

items.example: The suffix yields stateless for people outside any state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出 stateless，指不属于任何国家的人。

items.example: The suffix yields nationalism from the first half.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由前半造出 nationalism。

latinEntries.structure: nasci, natus sum (deponent verb, third conjugation)

definition_zh: 相应地；对应地；同步地；按相称的幅度
definition_en: in a way that matches another change or item, so that the two move or stand together, without saying that one causes the other
core_image: 双栏账本左右两栏始终齐平，左边添一行，右边也跟着添一行
scene: 双栏账本左边记支出，右边记余额，左边添一行，右边跟着添一行。 Output rose by a tenth and, correspondingly, employment rose by the same amount.
sceneCN: 这里指两处变化同步同幅（第 1 个义项：同步变化）；句意为产量增加了一成，就业也相应地增加了同样的幅度。场景要点：双栏账本、始终齐平的行数、同步添上的记录。

pos.zh: 相应地；对应地；同步地

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「共同回应」的动词构成，义为「相符、通信」
由对应动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「相符、通信」
由对应动词的现在分词加表示人或物的名词尾构成，义为「通信记者、对应物」
由对应动词的现在分词加形容词词尾构成，义为「相应的」

senses.title: A change matched by another change
senses.definition: marks a second change that keeps pace with the one just described, in direction and in rough amount
senses.definitionCN: 标出与前述变化同向、同幅的第二处变化
senses.example: Demand for cooling rose in July; energy use rose correspondingly.
senses.exampleCN: 七月制冷需求上升，能源消耗也相应上升。
senses.why: Respondere is to answer back, and two things that correspond answer each other, one movement meeting another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语动词意为「回应」，彼此对应的东西在互相回应，一处变动迎上另一处变动。

senses.title: A match in amount
senses.definition: used where the second quantity is not merely parallel but proportioned to the first, larger with larger and smaller with smaller
senses.definitionCN: 第二项不只是并行，而是与第一项相称，前者大后者也大，前者小后者也小
senses.example: Costs were cut by a fifth, and the staff was reduced correspondingly.
senses.exampleCN: 成本削减了五分之一，人员也相应裁减。
senses.why: Proportion is the strictest form of correspondence, and the word can carry it without naming a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 比例是对应关系里最严格的一种，这个词不必点明比率也能带上它。

senses.title: Sentence-initial in formal writing
senses.definition: placed first in a report or paper to announce that the matching change follows
senses.definitionCN: 置于报告或论文的句首，宣告与之相称的另一处变化随后出现
senses.example: Correspondingly, the second group showed a smaller rise.
senses.exampleCN: 相应地，第二组显示出较小的升幅。
senses.why: Written comparison needs a visible joint, and the opener supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 书面比较需要看得见的接缝，句首位置正好提供。

senses.title: The parenthesis inside the clause
senses.definition: set between commas so that the matching item is slipped in without stopping the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 用逗号夹在句中，把对应项轻轻塞入而不打断句子
senses.example: The northern route, correspondingly, takes two days longer.
senses.exampleCN: 相应地，北线要多走两天。
senses.why: Inside the clause the word works as a quiet aside rather than a signpost.
senses.whyCN: 放在小句内部，这个词是安静的旁注，而不是路标。

senses.title: The manner of adjusting
senses.definition: in final position with verbs of change, it says that the action was carried out to the matching degree
senses.definitionCN: 处于句末并与变化类动词连用，说明动作是按相称的幅度实施的
senses.example: When the tariff changed, the prices at the pump moved correspondingly.
senses.exampleCN: 关税变动之后，加油站的油价也相应变动。
senses.why: Final position puts the word inside the predicate, so it describes how the change was made.
senses.whyCN: 句末位置把这个词放进谓语，于是它描述变动是如何进行的。

senses.title: A structural counterpart
senses.definition: used of items that answer one another across two lists or systems, where the matching is one of position rather than of amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于两份清单或两套体系之间彼此对应的项目，对应的是位置而不是数量
senses.example: Each province has a correspondingly named office in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 每个省在首都都有一个名称相应的办事处。
senses.why: Correspondence is not only of size; two systems can mirror each other in structure.
senses.whyCN: 对应不只发生在大小上；两套体系可以在结构上互为镜像。

senses.title: Not a claim of cause
senses.definition: the boundary against the result words: correspondingly says the two moved together, not that one made the other move
senses.definitionCN: 与结果类词的分界：这个词说两者一起动，而不是一个使另一个动
senses.example: Correspondingly says the two moved together; consequently says one caused the other.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词说两者一同变动；表示客观结果的词才说一个造成了另一个。
senses.why: Matching is a relation of shape, and shape can be read without any causal arrow.
senses.whyCN: 相称是一种形状上的关系，读这种关系不必加上因果箭头。

senses.title: Not the same as respectively
senses.definition: the boundary against respectively: that word pairs the items of two lists in order, while this word pairs changes in size
senses.definitionCN: 与「分别地」的分界：那个词按顺序把两份清单逐项配对，这个词把两处变化的幅度配对
senses.example: Respectively pairs items in order; correspondingly pairs changes in size.
senses.exampleCN: 「分别地」按顺序配项目，这个词按大小配变化。
senses.why: Order and degree are different kinds of pairing, and English keeps separate words for them.
senses.whyCN: 顺序与幅度是两种不同的配对，英语为它们分别留了词。

intro.en: Correspondingly is corresponding plus -ly. Correspond comes from Medieval Latin correspondere, to answer together, built on com- together and respondere, to answer, itself re- back and spondere to promise. Two things correspond when each answers the other.
intro.cn: 这个词由形容词加副词词尾构成。动词来自中世纪拉丁语 correspondere「一同回应」，由 com-「共同」与 respondere「回答」构成，而 respondere 又是 re-「回」加 spondere「许诺」。两物相符，就是各自回应对方。

items.en: Spondere meant to promise or pledge, and it stands behind the English word for a spouse, a promised person.
items.cn: 这个词意为许诺、保证，英语里表示配偶的词也由它而来，原指「被许诺的人」。

items.en: Re- plus spondere made a verb of answering in return, as a promise answers a promise.
items.cn: re- 加 spondere 构成动词，意为回过来作答，像许诺回应许诺。

items.en: Com- plus respondere meant to answer together, and so to be in harmony or agreement.
items.cn: com- 加 respondere 意为一同回应，因而指彼此和谐、相符。

items.en: English took the verb for things that answer one another, and also for the exchange of letters.
items.cn: 英语借来这个动词，既指彼此回应的东西，也指书信往来。

items.en: The adverb marks a matching change or item; the exact date of its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词用来标出相称的变化或项目；其首次使用的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Tables and technical reports made it a standard word for two quantities that move in step.
items.cn: 表格与技术报告使它成为描述两个量同步变动的标准用词。

note.en: The first group shares the answering stem, with one word from an unrelated family; the second holds the words it is most often mixed up with.
note.cn: 第一组共享「回应」这一词干，另有一个来自无关词族的词；第二组是常与它弄混的几个词。

entries.definition: To match another thing, or to exchange letters with someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指与另一物相符，也指与某人通信。

entries.definition: A match between two sets, or the letters exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 指两组之间的相符，也指往来的书信。

entries.definition: A reporter based in a place, or a thing that matches another.
entries.definitionCN: 指驻某地的记者，也指与另一物相对应者。

entries.definition: Matching or analogous to something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指与另一物相应的、类似的。

entries.definition: From Latin roborare, to make strong like oak, not from respondere; it means to confirm a claim with evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「使如橡木般坚固」，不是「回应」；意为用证据证实某一说法。

entries.definition: Marks an action adjusted to the facts just given.
entries.definitionCN: 标记依前述事实作出的调整。

entries.definition: Pairs the items of two lists one to one, in the order given.
entries.definitionCN: 把两份清单的项目按所给顺序逐一配对。

entries.definition: In a way that keeps a stated ratio between the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以各部分之间保持明确比率的方式。

entries.definition: In the same way, often of a similar action rather than a matched quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 以同样的方式，常用于类似的动作而非相称的数量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin verb of answering back, the real correspondence family, and the two-column ledger.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「回话」的动词、真实的对应该词族，以及那本双栏账本。

normal.en: Respondere is to answer back, and things that correspond answer each other.
normal.cn: 词根意为「回应」，彼此对应的东西就是在互相回应。

normal.en: Two columns, one movement: the word keeps them level without saying which pushed which.
normal.cn: 两栏、一次变动：这个词让两边保持齐平，却不说谁推动了谁。

normal.en: It loves verbs of change: rise, fall, increase, adjust, vary.
normal.cn: 它偏爱变化类动词：升、降、增、调、变。

normal.en: Respectively lists in order; correspondingly moves in step. One is a roll call, the other a dance.
normal.cn: 「分别地」按顺序点名；这个词同步移动。一个是点名，一个是同行。

normal.en: The word adds no cause; it only reports a matching size.
normal.cn: 这个词不加因果，只报告一个相称的幅度。

abstract.en: Two things can keep step without one leading the other.
abstract.cn: 两样东西可以同步而行，而不必谁领着谁。

abstract.en: A pair is a promise that neither side will move alone.
abstract.cn: 成对，就是一种谁也不单独移动的约定。

abstract.en: Matching is a relation of size, and size can be measured but not blamed.
abstract.cn: 相称是一种大小上的关系，大小可以测量，却无从责怪。

examples.en: The temperature fell, and the pressure in the tank fell correspondingly.
examples.cn: 温度下降，罐内压力也相应下降。

examples.en: Correspondingly, the later chapters give less space to the early period.
examples.cn: 相应地，后面几章给早期阶段的篇幅更少。

examples.en: As the sample grew, the margin of error shrank correspondingly.
examples.cn: 随着样本增大，误差范围也相应缩小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「考瑞斯旁丁利」——两栏账本一起长，左添一行右也添一行：相应地

root: 拉丁语 spondere「许诺」→ respondere「回应」（re-「回」＋spondere）→ 中世纪拉丁语 correspondere「一同回应」→ 英语 correspond → corresponding，再加副词词尾构成。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses vary what is paired and where the word stands: a matching change, a proportioned amount, the written opener, the parenthesis, the manner at the end, a structural counterpart, the boundary against causal words, and the boundary against the listing word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项改变的是「配什么」与「站在哪里」：同步变化、相称幅度、书面句首、句中插入、句末方式、结构对应项、与因果词的分界、与列举词的分界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two columns of a ledger stay level, and a line added on the left brings a line on the right.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本的两栏始终齐平，左边添一行，右边就跟着添一行。

branches.en: THE MATCHED CHANGE: the two move together, and the size of one sets the size of the other.
branches.cn: 相称的变化：两者同步而动，一处的幅度决定另一处的幅度。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN JOINT: at the head of the sentence, or slipped inside it.
branches.cn: 书面接缝：或置于句首，或嵌进句中。

branches.en: THE MANNER AT THE END: the action is carried out to the matching degree.
branches.cn: 句末的方式：动作按相称的幅度实施。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURAL COUNTERPART: one list answers another in position.
branches.cn: 结构对应项：一份清单在位置上回应另一份。

branches.en: THE TWO BOUNDARIES: no causal arrow, and no simple roll call of items.
branches.cn: 两条边界：不加因果箭头，也不是逐项点名。

intro.en: Correspondingly is a Latin verb of answering back with a particle in front, an adjective ending and an English adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个表示「回应」的拉丁动词，前面带小品词，后面套形容词词尾与英语副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies spondere and respondere; Medieval Latin supplies correspondere, and English supplies correspond, corresponding and the endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 spondere 与 respondere；中世纪拉丁语提供了 correspondere，英语提供了 correspond、corresponding 与词尾。

items.example: The verb is the promise inside the answer.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是「回应」里那一半许诺。

items.example: It turns the promise into an answer given back.
items.exampleCN: 它把许诺变成回过来的作答。

items.example: The verb names an answer given to an answer.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指对回答作出的回答。

items.example: The compound names two things answering each other.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指两物彼此回应。

items.example: English adds the letter-writing sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上「书信往来」这一义。

items.example: The participle becomes an adjective of matching.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为表示「相称」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective and the noun of the matching thing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示对应之物的形容词与名词。

items.example: It forms the noun of correspondence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「相符」的名词。

items.example: It makes the adverb of matching change.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「相称变化」的副词。

derivatives.zh: 由中世纪拉丁语「共同回应」的动词构成，义为「相符、通信」
由对应动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「相符、通信」
由对应动词的现在分词加表示人或物的名词尾构成，义为「通信记者」
由对应动词的现在分词加形容词词尾构成，义为「相应的」

definition_zh: 有同情心的；出于怜悯的；温和体恤的；（假期、宽免等）因家庭急难而特许的
definition_en: feeling or showing sympathy for people who are suffering, and wishing to help them
core_image: 一位医生查房时先坐在床沿，问的不是指标而是病人昨夜睡得怎样，手里的病历一直合着
scene: 重症病房里，医生把病历夹合上放到一边，先问病人昨晚疼得能不能睡着。 The compassionate doctor sat on the edge of the bed and asked about the night before any question about test results.
sceneCN: 这里 compassionate 形容「对他人疾苦敏锐并愿意体恤的」（第 1 个义项：对他人苦难敏感而温情的）；句意为这位有同情心的医生坐在床沿，先问昨夜的情况，再谈检查结果。可辨识物件：合上的病历夹、病床床沿、监护仪、夜灯。

pos.zh: 有同情心的；出于怜悯的；体恤的

collocations.zh: 因家庭急难而准予的特别假
基于人道理由的（申请）依据
怜悯性释放（因重病或丧亲而提前释放）
温和保守主义（政治用语）

senses.title: Sensitive to other people's pain
senses.definition: describing a person who notices other people's suffering and feels for them
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人能察觉他人的痛苦并为之动情
senses.example: The compassionate doctor sat on the edge of the bed and asked about the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这位有同情心的医生坐在床沿，先问昨夜的情况。
senses.why: The adjective simply carries the noun's feeling into description: the person is full of shared suffering.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是把名词里的那份情感带进描述：这个人心中满是与人共担的苦。

senses.title: Driven by pity
senses.definition: describing an action taken because someone's suffering has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 形容因察觉到他人受苦而采取的行动
senses.example: A compassionate refusal is better than a careless yes.
senses.exampleCN: 出于怜悯的拒绝，胜过轻率的答应。
senses.why: When the word moves from the person to the act, it marks the motive behind the act.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从人移到行为上，它标出的是行为背后的动机。

senses.title: Gentle in manner
senses.titleCN: 语气与做法温和体贴的
senses.definition: describing words or handling that avoid adding humiliation to an already painful situation
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞或处理方式不再给本就痛苦的处境添上羞辱
senses.example: She gave the news in a compassionate voice, without any blame in it.
senses.exampleCN: 她用体恤的语气告知消息，话里没有一丝责备。
senses.why: Compassion is not only felt but delivered; the manner of delivery can wound or spare, so the word describes tone as well.
senses.whyCN: 同情不只要被感受到，还要被传达出来；传达方式可以伤人也可以护人，所以这个词也形容语气。

senses.title: Granted for a family emergency
senses.definition: describing leave or absence allowed because of a death, illness or crisis in the family
senses.definitionCN: 形容因家人去世、重病或突发变故而被批准的假期
senses.example: He was given three days of compassionate leave after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，他获准三天急难假。
senses.why: Workplace rules borrowed the word for the one situation in which an employer is expected to put a person before a schedule.
senses.whyCN: 职场规章借用了这个词，专指雇主被期待把人排在日程之前的那种情形。

senses.title: Allowed on humane grounds
senses.definition: describing a release, transfer or exception granted because of severe personal hardship
senses.definitionCN: 形容因个人处境极为艰难而获准的释放、转院或例外
senses.example: Prisoners nearing death may apply for compassionate release.
senses.exampleCN: 临近死亡的囚犯可以申请人道释放。
senses.why: Law keeps a narrow door for cases where strict application would be cruel, and the word names that door.
senses.whyCN: 法律为严格适用会显得残忍的情形留了一道窄门，这个词就是那道门的名字。

senses.title: Care that includes feeling
senses.definition: describing treatment that attends to distress as well as to the clinical task
senses.definitionCN: 形容在完成医疗任务之外也照顾到痛苦的照护
senses.example: Compassionate care begins with asking what the patient is most afraid of.
senses.exampleCN: 有温度的照护，从问病人最害怕什么开始。
senses.why: Care work made the adjective a standard of quality, not merely a compliment.
senses.whyCN: 照护行业把这个形容词变成了质量标准，而不只是一句称赞。

senses.title: Merciful in religious language
senses.titleCN: 宗教语境中慈悲为怀的
senses.definition: in religious writing, describing a mercy that extends to all beings without condition
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教文献中，形容无条件施及一切众生的慈悲
senses.example: The tradition describes a compassionate presence that turns towards every creature.
senses.exampleCN: 这一传统描述一种转向一切生灵的慈悲临在。
senses.why: The oldest use of the family is religious, and the adjective still carries that wide, unconditional reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个词族最古老的用法是宗教性的，形容词也仍带着那种无边的、无条件的覆盖。

senses.title: Designed with hardship in mind
senses.titleCN: 制度设计上顾及疾苦的
senses.definition: describing a policy or institution built to soften the hardship it inevitably causes
senses.definitionCN: 形容某项政策或制度在设计中设法减轻它必然造成的困苦
senses.example: A compassionate policy explains the decision in plain language and offers an appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 体恤的政策用平实的语言解释决定，并提供申诉渠道。
senses.why: The word's final reach is structural: once compassion is expected of institutions, rules themselves are called compassionate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最后延伸到结构层面：一旦人们期待机构有同情心，规则本身也会被称作体恤的。

intro.en: Compassionate is the adjective formed from compassion with the Latin suffix -ate, 'having the quality of'. The noun and the adjective entered English within the same medieval period.
intro.cn: compassionate 是由 compassion 加拉丁后缀 -ate「具有……性质的」构成的形容词。名词与形容词都在中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Pati 'to suffer, endure' is the root; its participle passus also gives passion and passive. The deeper origin of pati is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 词根 pati 意为「受苦、忍受」；其分词是 passion 与 passive 的来源。pati 的更深来源属重构。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus pati formed compati, 'to suffer with', the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 pati 构成 compati「一同受苦」，这是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: The noun compassio named the state of shared feeling; English took the noun first and then built the adjective on it.
items.cn: 名词 compassio 指共感的状态；英语先借入名词，再据它造出形容词。

items.en: The ending -ate comes from Latin -atus, marking a person or thing that possesses the quality named by the stem.
items.cn: 词尾 -ate 来自拉丁 -atus，表示人或事物具有词干所指的性质。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the sixteenth century, first in religious prose and later in ordinary description of people and acts.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪出现于英语，最早见于宗教散文，后来才用于日常对人、对事的描述。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of the adjective is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root of pati has no agreed form, so any Indo-European shape for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个形容词最早的英语书证没有确切年代；pati 在拉丁语之前的词根也没有公认形式，凡给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that sit beside this one in the same Latin family or in the same sentence; group two holds adjectives with a similar warmth but a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词族、或在同一句里并列出现在的形容词；第二组是暖意相近但覆盖面不同的形容词。

entries.definition: From the same suffering participle but describing intense enthusiasm or love, not tenderness towards pain.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「受苦」分词，却形容炽烈的热情或爱，而非对痛苦的温柔。

entries.definition: The noun names the feeling; the adjective names the person or act that has it. The pair is a regular noun-adjective set, not two separate ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指这份情感，形容词指具有这份情感的人或行为。两者是常规的名词—形容词配对，并非两个不同概念。

entries.definition: From the present participle of the same verb, 'enduring'; a patient bears pain while a compassionate person responds to it.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该动词的现在分词，意为「忍受着」；病人承受痛苦，而有同情心的人回应痛苦。

entries.definition: Built on the Latin verb for suffering as well but in the sense of enduring together; its modern meaning is 'able to work together', which has lost the pain entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 同样建于表示「受苦」的拉丁动词，原义为「能一同承受」；现代义为「能相容并用」，痛感已完全消失。

entries.definition: Attentive to another's practical needs; it can be shown by good service alone, without any reflection on suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 留意他人实际需要；仅靠周到的服务就能体现，不必对痛苦有所体察。

entries.definition: Quick to feel for another's trouble and to express that feeling; it stops at the feeling, where compassionate goes on to help.
entries.definitionCN: 容易为他人的困难动情并表达出来；它止于情感，而 compassionate 会继续走向援手。

entries.definition: Treating people or animals in a way that avoids unnecessary suffering; it is a minimum standard, while compassionate is a warmth beyond the minimum.
entries.definitionCN: 以不造成不必要痛苦的方式对待人或动物；它是最低标准，而 compassionate 是超出最低标准的热度。

entries.definition: Gentle and careful in touch or speech; it describes the manner only, not the motive of noticing another's pain.
entries.definitionCN: 在触碰或言语上轻柔小心；它只描述方式，不含察觉他人痛苦的动机。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real noun behind the adjective, the real workplace phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、形容词背后真实的名词、真实的职场说法与真实的同族词。

normal.en: The noun compassion means suffering together; the adjective simply says that a person or act has that quality.
normal.cn: 名词 compassion 意为「一同受苦」，形容词只是说明某人或某行为具备这种性质。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks possession of a quality, the same ending that turns fortune into fortunate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 表示「具有某种性质」，与把「运气」变成「幸运的」用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: Workplace phrases pin the word down: compassionate leave, compassionate grounds, compassionate release.
normal.cn: 职场说法把这个词固定下来：急难假、人道理由、怜悯性释放。

normal.en: Hospitals use it as a quality standard: compassionate care is assessed alongside technical competence.
normal.cn: 医院把它当作质量标准：有温度的照护与技术能力一起被考核。

normal.en: The contrast to hold in mind is passionate, from the same root but about heat rather than tenderness.
normal.cn: 要记住的对照是 passionate，同出一个词根，但说的是炽烈而非温柔。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that slows down before it touches a bruise.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在碰到淤青之前先放慢了速度。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open a few extra seconds for someone carrying too much.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门为提着太多东西的人多开了几秒。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that lowers itself when the news is bad.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音在坏消息面前自觉放低。

examples.en: The university granted her compassionate leave for the funeral.
examples.cn: 学校批准她因葬礼申请的急难假。

examples.en: A compassionate manager asks what happened before asking when the work will be done.
examples.cn: 体恤的管理者先问发生了什么，再问工作何时完成。

examples.en: The report recommends compassionate release for prisoners with terminal illness.
examples.cn: 报告建议对绝症囚犯实行人道释放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「共同 + 受苦 + 具有这种性质」——心里装着别人的痛，言行就自然温和体恤

root: 拉丁 compassio「同感、怜悯」+ 后缀 -ate（具有……性质的）；compassio 出自 compati「一同受苦」= com-（共同）+ pati（受苦）。深层词根不确定，印欧形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same quality applied to different things: first a person, then an act, then a tone, then a leave, a legal exception, a style of care, a religious mercy, and finally a policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的是同一种性质落在不同对象上：先落在人身上，再落到行为、语气、假期、法律例外、照护风格、宗教慈悲，最后落到政策上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that slows down before it reaches a place that hurts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在伸向疼痛之处前先放慢了速度。

branches.en: PERSON AND MOTIVE: the one who notices, and the act that follows from noticing.
branches.cn: 人与动机：先是察觉的人，再是由察觉引出的行为。

branches.en: DELIVERY: the same feeling shows in how the words are said.
branches.cn: 传达：同一份情感体现在话怎么说出口。

branches.en: TIME AND EXEMPTION: employers give days, the law opens a narrow door.
branches.cn: 时间与例外：雇主给出几天假，法律开出一道窄门。

branches.en: CARE AND MERCY: a clinical standard on one side, an unconditional religious reach on the other.
branches.cn: 照护与慈悲：一边是临床标准，一边是无条件的宗教覆盖。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: the quality moves from people into the design of rules.
branches.cn: 结构：这种性质从人身上移入规则的设计。

intro.en: Compassionate is built from a Latin noun plus the suffix -ate, and both parts recur in many English words.
intro.cn: compassionate 由一个拉丁名词加后缀 -ate 构成，两部分都在大量英语词中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The stem carries shared suffering; -ate marks possession of a quality, as in fortunate and passionate.
latinIntro.cn: 词干带着「共同受苦」的意思；-ate 表示具有某种性质，如 fortunate 与 passionate 中的用法。

items.example: The prefix makes the feeling shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀让情感成为共享的。

items.example: The root supplies the pain.
The noun underlies the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成描述。

items.example: The compassionate doctor sat on the edge of the bed.
items.exampleCN: 这位有同情心的医生坐在床沿。

items.example: She refused compassionately.
The ward was known for its compassionateness.
An uncompassionate reply closed the conversation.
items.exampleCN: 一句冷漠的回应终止了对话。

latinEntries.structure: pati, passus sum (verb, deponent, third conjugation)

definition_zh: 教育学；教学法；关于教学与学习方法的理论与实践
definition_en: the theory and practice of teaching
core_image: 一位老师把整间教室的桌椅重新摆成半圆，让每个孩子都能看见别人的眼睛，再开始提问
scene: 师范学院的课堂上，学生先设计一堂课，再互相扮演学生，最后拆解刚才每一步为什么有效。 The seminar examined pedagogy by having students teach a lesson and then dissect it.
sceneCN: 这里 pedagogy 指关于教学方法的理论与实践（第 1 个义项：教学的艺术与学问）；句意为研讨课让学生先上一堂课，再拆解它，以此来考察教学法。

pos.zh: 教育学；教学法（不可数，指理论、学问或方法体系）
某一教师或某一学科的教学风格与做法

collocations.zh: 评价方式背后的教学观

derivatives.zh: 教师；（贬义）教书匠（由希腊语「护送男孩的家奴」经拉丁与法语进入英语，从照看孩子的人转指教师）
教学法的（由希腊语「教学」词干加表示「属于」的希腊后缀构成，经拉丁与法语进入英语）
教学法的；教育学的（由 pedagogic 加表示「属于」的英语后缀构成）
从教学法角度（由 pedagogical 加表示「方式」的后缀构成）
教学法研究（由 pedagogic 加表示「学问」的后缀构成，指教学法的系统研究）

senses.title: The art and science of teaching
senses.definition: the study and practice of how teaching is done, treated as both a craft and a field of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 对教学如何进行的学问与实践，既被视为技艺，也被视为知识领域
senses.example: The seminar examined pedagogy by having students teach a lesson and then dissect it.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课让学生先上一堂课，再拆解它，以此来考察教学法。
senses.why: The Greek word first named the slave who led a boy to school; the modern word names the study of that leading, now done by teachers themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初命名送男孩上学的家奴；现代词则命名对「引导」这件事的研究，如今由教师自己来做。

senses.title: The theory of instruction
senses.definition: a systematic account of how instruction should be designed and why it works
senses.definitionCN: 关于教学应当如何设计、为何有效的系统论述
senses.example: Her book sets out a pedagogy grounded in how novices actually think.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书提出一种以初学者实际如何思考为基础的教学理论。
senses.why: Theory turns practice into something that can be argued about, tested and taught to new teachers.
senses.whyCN: 理论把实践变成可争论、可检验、可教给新教师的东西。

senses.title: The method or practice of teaching
senses.definition: the concrete choices a teacher makes in a classroom, such as grouping, questioning and pacing
senses.definitionCN: 教师在课堂上做出的具体选择，如分组、提问与节奏
senses.example: His pedagogy changed when he moved the desks into a circle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把课桌摆成圆形后，教学法也随之改变。
senses.why: Here the word is closest to practice: it names what a teacher actually does, not what a journal article recommends.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词最贴近实践：它命名教师实际怎么做，而非期刊论文建议怎么做。

senses.title: Critical pedagogy
senses.definition: an approach that treats teaching as a way of questioning power and inviting students to act
senses.definitionCN: 把教学视为质疑权力、邀请学生行动的一种路径
senses.example: Critical pedagogy asks whose knowledge the textbook leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 批判教育学追问教科书漏掉了谁的知识。
senses.why: A named school within the field, it joins the word to a political commitment rather than to technique alone.
senses.whyCN: 这是领域内部一个有名字的流派，它把教学法与政治承诺结合，而非只与技术结合。

senses.title: The pedagogy of the oppressed
senses.definition: a teaching practice that begins from the experience of the oppressed and aims at their liberation
senses.definitionCN: 从受压迫者的经验出发、以其解放为目标的教学实践
senses.example: The course read the pedagogy of the oppressed alongside folk-school records.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程把受压迫者教育学与民间学校档案并读。
senses.why: The phrase turns teaching into a political act, so pedagogy here is not neutral method but a stance.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把教学变成政治行动，因此这里的教学法不是中立方法，而是一种立场。

senses.title: Subject-specific pedagogy
senses.definition: the particular ways of teaching a subject, such as history pedagogy or mathematics pedagogy
senses.definitionCN: 教授某一学科的特有方式，如历史教学法或数学教学法
senses.example: Mathematics pedagogy has its own debates about symbols and proof.
senses.exampleCN: 数学教学法有自己关于符号与证明的争论。
senses.why: Each discipline has its own ways of making knowledge visible, so the word attaches to the subject.
senses.whyCN: 每门学科都有让知识可见的特有方式，因此这个词会接上具体学科。

senses.title: Curriculum design as pedagogy
senses.titleCN: 课程设计层面的教学法
senses.definition: the arrangement of content, sequence and assessment understood as part of teaching rather than as administration
senses.definitionCN: 把内容、顺序与评价的安排理解为教学的一部分，而非行政事务
senses.example: The new curriculum was praised for its pedagogy, not its list of topics.
senses.exampleCN: 新课程受到称赞的是它的教学安排，而不是主题清单。
senses.why: Design carries teaching: what is placed first and what is tested tells students what kind of learning is expected.
senses.whyCN: 设计本身承载教学：先放什么、考什么，都在告诉学生期待何种学习。

senses.title: Abstract: shaping of learning
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对学习的有意塑造
senses.definition: any deliberate arrangement that shapes how someone learns, inside or outside a classroom
senses.definitionCN: 任何有意安排、塑造某人如何学习的方式，无论课堂内外
senses.example: A good museum label has its own pedagogy.
senses.exampleCN: 一块好的博物馆说明牌也有自己的教学法。
senses.why: At its widest the word names the intention behind an arrangement, not a profession or a syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个词命名安排背后的意图，而非职业或大纲。

intro.en: Pedagogy comes from Greek paidagogia, 'attendance on a boy', built on pais 'child' and agein 'to lead'. The modern sense of theory of teaching is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pedagogy 来自希腊语 paidagogia「照看男孩」，由 pais「孩子」与 agein「引导」构成。现代「教学理论」义要晚得多。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pais, with the stem paid-, meant 'child, boy'. The same stem appears in pediatrics, the care of children.
items.cn: pais 的词干是 paid-，意为「孩子、男孩」。同一词干也出现在 pediatrics（儿科）中。

items.en: Agein meant 'to lead, drive'. It supplies the second half of the word and the idea of guiding someone.
items.cn: agein 意为「引导、驱赶」。它提供这个词的后半段与「引导某人」的意象。

items.en: Paidagogos named the household slave who escorted a boy to school and supervised him on the way. The word named a person, not a theory.
items.cn: paidagogos 指护送男孩上学、沿途照看的家奴。这个词命名的是人，不是理论。

items.en: Paidagogia meant 'attendance on a boy', the work of that slave. In ancient Greek it did not mean the theory of teaching.
items.cn: paidagogia 意为「照看男孩」，是那个家奴的工作。在古希腊语中，它不指教学理论。

items.en: Latin borrowed paedagogus and paedagogia, and French pédagogie carried the word into educational writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 paedagogus 与 paedagogia，法语 pédagogie 把这个词带进教育写作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): English pedagogy is recorded from the sixteenth century, but the modern sense of the theory of teaching became common only later.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语 pedagogy 自十六世纪有记录，但「教学理论」这一现代义后来才通行。

note.en: Group one separates the word from its relative for the teacher and from two Greek look-alikes; group two holds the near names for teaching as a field.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与指教师的亲属词、以及两个希腊语形近词分开；第二组是把教学作为领域的近邻名称。

entries.definition: The teacher; the noun for the person, while pedagogy names the theory or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 教师；这个名词指人，而 pedagogy 指理论或实践。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching methods; the adjective describes what pedagogy names.
entries.definitionCN: 与教学方法有关的；形容词描述 pedagogy 所命名的东西。

entries.definition: From pais 'child' plus iatreia 'healing'; it shares the child stem but has nothing to do with teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pais「孩子」加 iatreia「治疗」构成；它共享「孩子」词干，却与教学无关。

entries.definition: From dēmos 'people' plus agein 'lead': leading the people by appeal to emotion. It shares agein but not pais.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dēmos「人民」加 agein「引导」构成：以情绪诉求引导民众。它共享 agein，却不共享 pais。

entries.definition: The everyday name for the activity; pedagogy adds theory, method and reflection.
entries.definitionCN: 这项活动的日常名称；pedagogy 加上理论、方法与反思。

entries.definition: The act of delivering lessons or directions; it stresses transmission more than pedagogy does.
entries.definitionCN: 传递课程或指令的行为；它比 pedagogy 更强调传递。

entries.definition: The study of teaching methods, from Greek didaskein 'to teach'; it overlaps with pedagogy but is often narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 对教学方法的研究，来自希腊语 didaskein「教」；与 pedagogy 重叠，但通常更窄。

entries.definition: The broad process and system of educating; pedagogy is the teaching side of it, not the whole institution.
entries.definitionCN: 教育的广义过程与制度；pedagogy 是其中教学的一面，而非整个制度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real Greek words and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的希腊词与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pais means child, so pedagogy begins with the young person being led.
normal.cn: pais 意为孩子，所以 pedagogy 从被引导的年轻人开始。

normal.en: Agein means lead, so the second half is the act of guiding, not filling.
normal.cn: agein 意为引导，所以后半段是引导的动作，不是填充。

normal.en: The ancient paidagogos was a slave escort, which is why the word first named a person rather than a method.
normal.cn: 古代的 paidagogos 是护送的家奴，所以这个词最初命名人，而非方法。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the schools: critical pedagogy, subject pedagogy, classroom pedagogy.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出流派：批判教育学、学科教学法、课堂教学法。

normal.en: Pediatrics shares pais but not agein, so it is about children's health, not teaching.
normal.cn: pediatrics 共享 pais 却不共享 agein，所以它关乎儿童健康，与教学无关。

abstract.en: Picture a room rearranged into a half circle so every child can see every other child's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子被摆成半圆，让每个孩子都能看见别人的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a lesson taken apart on a table like a clock, each step laid beside the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一堂课像钟表一样被拆在桌上，每一步都摆在下一步旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp carried ahead of a small figure on a dark road to school.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯在暗路上走在一个小身影前面，通往学校。

examples.en: The department treats pedagogy as a research field, not as a set of tricks.
examples.cn: 这个系把教学法当作研究领域，而非一套窍门。

examples.en: Her pedagogy gives students time to be wrong before they are corrected.
examples.cn: 她的教学法给学生留出犯错的时间，再加以纠正。

examples.en: The report compares the pedagogy of online and face-to-face courses.
examples.cn: 报告比较在线课程与面授课程的教学法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派达 够 吉」——牵着孩子走向学堂的那门学问 → 教学法

root: 希腊 pais「孩子」+ agein「引导」→ paidagogos「护送男孩的家奴」→ paidagogia「照看男孩」；现代「教学理论」义为后起。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with teaching as a craft and a field, then move to theory, classroom practice, critical schools, liberation, subject methods, curriculum design and finally any deliberate shaping of learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把教学看作技艺与领域，再转到理论、课堂实践、批判流派、解放、学科方法、课程设计，最后是任何对学习的有意塑造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp carried ahead of a child on the road to school, then the same road studied by teachers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯在孩子上学的路上走在前头，随后这条路由教师来研究。

branches.en: CRAFT AND CLASSROOM: teaching as knowledge, then as the concrete choices made in a room.
branches.cn: 技艺与课堂：教学作为知识，再作为课堂中的具体选择。

branches.en: THEORY: instruction explained systematically so that it can be argued and tested.
branches.cn: 理论：对教学作系统解释，使其可被争论与检验。

branches.en: CRITICAL AND LIBERATING: named schools that make teaching a political stance.
branches.cn: 批判与解放：有名字的流派，把教学变成政治立场。

branches.en: SUBJECT AND SEQUENCE: methods specific to a discipline, and design as a form of teaching.
branches.cn: 学科与顺序：特定学科的方法，以及作为教学形式的设计。

branches.en: THE INTENTION: any arrangement that deliberately shapes how someone learns.
branches.cn: 意图：任何有意塑造某人如何学习的安排。

intro.en: Pedagogy is Greek from top to bottom: a child, a leader and the slave who walked between them.
intro.cn: pedagogy 从头到尾都是希腊语：一个孩子、一位引导者，以及走在两者之间的家奴。

latinIntro.en: Greek pais and agein build paidagogos and paidagogia; English adds pedagogy, pedagogue and pedagogical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 pais 与 agein 构成 paidagogos 与 paidagogia；英语再加 pedagogy、pedagogue 与 pedagogical。

items.example: The first element names the learner.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分命名学习者。

items.example: The stem appears in pediatrics too.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也出现在 pediatrics 中。

items.example: The second element names the guiding.
Agogos turns the verb into a leader.
items.exampleCN: agogos 把动词变成引导者。

items.meaning: the slave who led a boy
items.example: The compound first named a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词最初命名人。

items.example: The noun named the slave's work.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名家奴的工作。

items.meaning: the theory and practice of teaching
items.example: The modern sense is much later.
The person sense survived.
The adjective describes the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述这一领域。

definition_zh: n. 传记作者，传记作家
definition_en: a person who writes the life story of another person
core_image: 档案室里堆满来信与旧照片，一个人正把散落的日期排成一条线
scene: 传记作者在档案馆里待了三年，只为查清一个日期。 The biographer spent three years in the archives to pin down a single date.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biographer 指为他人写传记的人；句意是传记作者为查清一个日期在档案里待了三年。

pos.zh: 传记作者；传记作家

senses.title: A writer of a life story
senses.definition: someone whose work is to tell the story of another person life in a book
senses.definitionCN: 以成书形式讲述他人一生的人
senses.example: Her biographer interviewed forty people who had known her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的传记作者采访了四十位认识她的人。
senses.why: Graphy means writing and bio means life, so a biographer is literally a life-writer.
senses.whyCN: graphy 意为书写，bio 意为生命，biographer 字面就是「书写生命的人」。

senses.title: A researcher who reconstructs a life
senses.definition: a scholar who works from letters, records and interviews to rebuild a life in detail
senses.definitionCN: 依据书信、档案与访谈细致重建某人一生的学者
senses.example: The biographer checked every claim against the parish register.
senses.exampleCN: 这位传记作者把每个说法都对照教区登记簿核对过。
senses.why: A life story is only as good as its evidence, so the writer is also an investigator.
senses.whyCN: 传记的质量取决于证据，因此写作者同时也是调查者。

intro.en: Biographer is Greek bios, life, plus graphein, to write, plus the agent ending -er.
intro.cn: biographer 是希腊语 bios（生命）加 graphein（书写），再接施事词尾 -er。

items.en: Bios means life, the first element in biology and biography.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biography 的第一构件。

items.en: Graphein means to scratch or write, the root of graph and paragraph.
items.cn: graphein 意为刻写，是 graph 与 paragraph 的词根。

items.en: Biographia names the writing of a life.
items.cn: biographia 指书写一生。

items.en: English biography settles as the name of the genre.
items.cn: 英语 biography 固定为这一体裁的名称。

items.en: The agent noun appears for the writer of such a book.
items.cn: 施事名词出现，指写这类书的人。

items.en: The word comes to name a recognised line of work.
items.cn: 这个词开始指一门被承认的职业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -graph- build; the near-meaning group runs from the writer of a life to the keeper of records.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -graph- 构造；近义组从「写一生的人」排到「保存记录的人」。

entries.definition: The written life of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 某人一生的成书记述。

entries.definition: Relating to a person life story.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人生平有关的。

entries.definition: A list of books and sources.
entries.definitionCN: 书目；参考书清单。

entries.definition: The study of the earth surface.
entries.definitionCN: 对地球表面的研究。

entries.definition: A person who studies and writes history.
entries.definitionCN: 研究与撰写历史的人。

entries.definition: A person who writes a memoir.
entries.definitionCN: 写回忆录的人。

entries.definition: A person who records events in order.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序记录事件的人。

entries.definition: A person who keeps a diary.
entries.definitionCN: 记日记的人。

normalIntro.en: Bio is life and graphy is writing, so a biographer is the one who writes a life.
normalIntro.cn: bio 是生命，graphy 是书写，biographer 就是书写一生的人。

normal.en: Bio- appears in biology, life science.
normal.cn: bio- 出现在 biology，即生命科学。

normal.en: Graph- appears in paragraph, something written.
normal.cn: graph- 出现在 paragraph，即可写出的段落。

normal.en: Add -er and you have the person doing the writing.
normal.cn: 加 -er 就是做书写这件事的人。

normal.en: A biographer needs letters, dates and witnesses.
normal.cn: 传记作者需要书信、日期与证人。

normal.en: One book, one life, and years of archives.
normal.cn: 一本书，一段人生，和数年档案。

abstract.en: A life rebuilt from paper.
abstract.cn: 用纸重建的一生。

abstract.en: Someone else carrying your dates.
abstract.cn: 替你保管日期的人。

abstract.en: A stranger who knows your childhood better than you.
abstract.cn: 比你更熟悉你童年的陌生人。

examples.en: Her biographer found a letter that changed the accepted story.
examples.cn: 她的传记作者找到一封信，改变了公认的说法。

examples.en: Every biographer faces the same problem: what to leave out.
examples.cn: 每个传记作者都面对同一个问题：该舍弃什么。

examples.en: He worked as a biographer before turning to fiction.
examples.cn: 他在转写小说之前从事传记写作。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ graph（写）+ er（人）——把一个人的一生写下来的人，就是传记作者。

root: 希腊 bios（生命）+ graphein（书写）+ -er（做……的人）

sensesIntro.en: The writer and the researcher are the same person seen twice: one at the desk, one in the archive.
sensesIntro.cn: 「写作者」与「考据者」是同一个人被看两次：一次坐在书桌前，一次待在档案里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters, photographs and dates spread across a desk until a life lines up
core.cn: 核心意象：来信、照片与日期铺满桌面，直到一生被排成一条线

branches.en: Forty interviews for one chapter.
branches.cn: 为一章做的四十次访谈。

branches.en: A manuscript with a life inside it.
branches.cn: 装着一生的手稿。

branches.en: A parish register checked twice.
branches.cn: 被核对两遍的教区登记簿。

branches.en: A footnote that took three years.
branches.cn: 花了三年才写成的一条脚注。

branches.en: Writing that must be proved before it is told.
branches.cn: 必须先被证实才能被讲述的书写。

intro.en: Biographer is two Greek roots and an English agent ending; the list below builds the writing vocabulary around it.
intro.cn: biographer 由两个希腊词根加一个英语施事词尾构成；下面列出围绕它的书写词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek graphein is to write, bios is life, and autos is self.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 graphein 意为书写，bios 意为生命，autos 意为自身。

definition_zh: 绘画；油画；画作；（上漆的）涂装
definition_en: the art or activity of making pictures with paint, a picture made in this way, or the act of coating a surface with paint
core_image: 一支笔蘸着湿颜料在布上走过，留下一条再也改不回原样的痕迹
scene: 展厅里，修复师在斜射灯下检查一幅画的裂纹，判断清漆是否该去掉。 The conservator examined the painting under raking light.
sceneCN: 这里 painting 指「一幅画作」（第 1 个义项：用颜料绘成的图画）；句意为修复师在斜射光下检查这幅画，判断裂纹与清漆状况。

pos.zh: 绘画（艺术或活动）；画作；涂装

derivatives.zh: paint + -er（人）→ 画家／油漆工；从「动作」转到「施事者」
paint + -ed（过去分词）→ 涂过漆的；从「动作」转到「状态」
paint + work（成品）→ 漆面；从「涂料」转到「涂装结果」
painter + -ly（形容词）→ 有绘画笔触感的；从「人」转到「画面质感」

senses.title: A painted picture
senses.definition: a picture made with paint, especially on canvas or panel
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料绘成的图画，尤指画在布面或木板上
senses.example: The conservator examined the painting under raking light.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师在斜射光下检查这幅画。
senses.why: The noun of result names the finished object: what the verb paint produces, treated as a thing that can hang on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 结果名词命名完成的物件：动词 paint 所产出之物，被当作可以挂上墙的东西。

senses.title: The art form
senses.definition: the art of making pictures with paint, considered as a discipline
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料作画的艺术，作为一门学科来看
senses.example: Painting is older than photography by many centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 绘画比摄影早了许多个世纪。
senses.why: The same result-noun can name the whole practice, because a body of works defines a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 同一个结果名词也能命名整个实践，因为一批作品就界定了一门学科。

senses.title: The act of painting
senses.definition: the activity or process of making a picture with paint
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料制作图画的行动或过程
senses.example: Painting takes patience before it takes skill.
senses.exampleCN: 作画先要耐心，然后才谈技巧。
senses.why: The verbal noun also names the ongoing action, not only its outcome; English -ing forms routinely hold both readings.
senses.whyCN: 动名词也命名进行中的动作，而不只是结果；英语 -ing 形式通常同时容纳两种读法。

senses.title: A school or period style
senses.definition: the characteristic style of a school, region or period
senses.definitionCN: 某个画派、地区或时期的典型风格
senses.example: Dutch painting of the golden age is full of reflected light.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金时代的荷兰绘画充满反射光。
senses.why: A mass of works made in one place and time shows shared habits, so the noun can name a style rather than one picture.
senses.whyCN: 一地一时的大量作品显出共同习惯，因此这个名词能命名一种风格，而非一幅画。

senses.title: A subject category
senses.definition: a genre defined by subject, as in portrait painting or landscape painting
senses.definitionCN: 按题材界定的画类，如肖像画或风景画
senses.example: Portrait painting paid better than landscape in his day.
senses.exampleCN: 在他那个年代，肖像画比风景画更赚钱。
senses.why: Genres are compounds built on the noun: the subject in front narrows the art form to one marketable kind.
senses.whyCN: 画类是以这个名词构成的复合词：前面的题材把艺术门类收窄为一种可售卖的类别。

senses.title: Paintwork on a surface
senses.definition: the coating of paint on a building or object
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或物件表面的涂料层
senses.example: The painting of the bridge takes six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的涂装要六周。
senses.why: Because the verb also means 'coat a surface', the noun can name the layer applied, not a picture at all.
senses.whyCN: 因为动词也指「涂覆表面」，名词便能命名所涂的层，与图画无关。

senses.title: The coating trade
senses.definition: the trade or industry of applying paint to surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 把涂料施于表面的行业
senses.example: Industrial painting moved to the new shed.
senses.exampleCN: 工业涂装搬到了新厂房。
senses.why: An activity repeated for hire becomes an industry, so the -ing noun names the trade as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 为报酬反复进行的活动会变成行业，因此 -ing 名词既命名动作，也命名行业。

senses.title: A medium or technique
senses.definition: a particular medium or technique, as in oil painting or watercolour painting
senses.definitionCN: 某种特定媒介或技法，如油画或水彩画
senses.example: She works in oil painting but teaches drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 她画油画，但教的是素描。
senses.why: The medium in front of the noun turns the art form into a technique: what the paint is made of changes how the picture is made.
senses.whyCN: 名词前的媒介把艺术门类变成一种技法：颜料由什么构成，改变了画如何被制作。

intro.en: Painting is the verbal noun of paint, recorded around 1200; paint came through Old French from Latin pingere, whose deeper root is reconstructed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: painting 是 paint 的动名词，约 1200 年有记录；paint 经古法语来自拉丁 pingere，其更早词根属重构。年代均为约数。

items.en: Reconstructed root *peig- meant 'to cut, mark by incision'; the step from 'decorate with cut marks' to 'decorate with colour' is presumed rather than attested.
items.cn: 重构词根 *peig- 意为「切、刻痕」；从「以刻痕装饰」到「以色彩装饰」的演变是推测，而非有直接书证。

items.en: Pingere meant 'to paint, represent in a picture, stain; embroider, tattoo'.
items.cn: pingere 意为「绘画、在图中表现、染色；刺绣、纹身」。

items.en: Old French peindre 'to paint' supplied the past participle peint, from which English paint derives.
items.cn: 古法语 peindre「绘画」提供过去分词 peint，英语 paint 由此而来。

items.en: English paint is recorded from the mid-thirteenth century, first for representing someone or something in paint.
items.cn: 英语 paint 自 13 世纪中叶有记录，最初指用颜料表现某人或某物。

items.en: Painting is recorded around 1200 for 'that which is painted, a picture'; by the late fourteenth century it also meant the art of depicting with paint.
items.cn: painting 约 1200 年有记录，指「被画成之物、图画」；到 14 世纪后期也指用颜料描绘的艺术。

items.en: From the general verb sense 'cover a surface with colour', the noun acquired the paintwork and trade senses.
items.cn: 从动词的一般义「用颜色覆盖表面」，名词获得了涂层与行业义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same paint- stock that differ in word class or result; group two holds words for pictures and surfaces made in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 paint- 词干、但词类或结果不同的词；第二组是用其他方式制作的图画与表面。

entries.definition: The person who paints; painting is the activity or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 作画或涂漆的人；painting 是活动或其产物。

entries.definition: To coat or depict, or the substance used; painting adds the result or activity suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 涂覆或描绘，或所用材料；painting 加上结果或活动后缀。

entries.definition: Describes a surface that has received paint; it is a participle, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已上漆的表面；是分词，而非名词。

entries.definition: Describes visible brushwork and a picture-like quality; it is a style judgement, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可见笔触与画面感；是风格判断，不是类别。

entries.definition: A picture made with lines, usually dry media; painting works with liquid colour and surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用线条、通常以干性媒材作的画；painting 使用液体颜料与表面。

entries.definition: Any visual representation, including photographs and prints; painting specifies the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 任何视觉再现，包括照片与版画；painting 限定媒介。

entries.definition: The woven surface for a painting, or a painting by metonymy; it names the support rather than the art.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画所用的织布表面，或以转喻指一幅画；命名的是支撑物而非艺术。

entries.definition: A layer of material covering a surface; it is the technical cousin of the paintwork sense.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖表面的材料层；是 painting 涂装义的技术近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paint + -ing: the activity or the thing made.
normal.cn: paint + -ing：活动，或做出来的东西。

normal.en: Latin pingere is the source, and the same stem gives picture and pigment.
normal.cn: 来源是拉丁 pingere，同一词干还给出 picture 与 pigment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: oil painting, portrait painting, the painting of the bridge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：油画、肖像画、桥梁涂装。

normal.en: The family runs paint, painter, painting, painted, paintwork and painterly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paint、painter、painting、painted、paintwork 与 painterly。

normal.en: A museum label says 'oil on canvas' but calls the object a painting.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签写「布面油画」，却把对象称作 painting。

abstract.en: Picture a wet stroke that cannot be undone without leaving a trace.
abstract.cn: 想象一道湿笔触，想撤掉总会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a flat surface becoming a window that is also an object.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平面变成既是窗又是物的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall and a canvas answering to the same action.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙与一块画布回应同一个动作。

examples.en: The painting was relined before the exhibition.
examples.cn: 这幅画在展览前做了托裱。

examples.en: Painting was taught alongside anatomy in the old academy.
examples.cn: 在旧式学院里，绘画与解剖学一起教授。

examples.en: The painting of the hall took longer than the carpentry.
examples.cn: 大厅的涂装比木工花的时间更长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paint（涂颜料）+ -ing」——涂出来的东西 → 画

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」经古法语 peindre、过去分词 peint 进入英语 paint（13 世纪中叶）；painting 约 1200 年出现，兼指画作、绘画艺术与涂装。更早词根拟为 *peig-「刻痕」，属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the finished picture to the art form, the act, a school, a genre, a painted surface, the coating trade and a specific medium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从完成的画作转到艺术门类、行为、画派、画类、涂层、涂装行业与具体媒介。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush loaded with wet pigment crosses the cloth and leaves a mark that cannot return to nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支蘸满湿颜料的笔走过布面，留下一条无法回到空白的痕迹。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: the result, hanging on a wall.
branches.cn: 画作：结果，挂在墙上。

branches.en: ART AND MEDIUM: the whole discipline, then one technique inside it.
branches.cn: 艺术与媒介：整门学科，然后是其中一种技法。

branches.en: THE ACT: the doing, which the same suffix also names.
branches.cn: 行为：正在做的过程，同一后缀也能命名它。

branches.en: SCHOOL AND GENRE: shared habits across works, then a subject category.
branches.cn: 画派与画类：作品间的共同习惯，然后是题材类别。

branches.en: THE SURFACE TRADE: coating an object, then the industry that does it for hire.
branches.cn: 表面行业：给物件上涂层，然后是为报酬做这件事的行业。

intro.en: Painting is a verb stem plus the noun suffix -ing, and the stem builds a family of people, results and styles.
intro.cn: painting 是动词词干加名词后缀 -ing，同一词干还构成指人、结果与风格的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere is the ancestor; it also yields picture, pigment and depict, all through the idea of marking a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 祖先是拉丁 pingere；它还给出 picture、pigment 与 depict，都经由「在表面留下痕迹」这一观念。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere
items.meaning: to colour a surface; to depict
items.example: They painted the door blue.
Building and painting use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: building 与 painting 用同一个词尾。

items.meaning: a picture; the art or act
items.example: The painting hangs in the north room.
The painter primed the wall.
The painted shutters were new.
items.exampleCN: 上过漆的百叶窗是新的。

items.meaning: the painted surface of an object
items.example: The paintwork was chipped at the edge.
The photograph has a painterly softness.
items.exampleCN: 这张照片有一种绘画般的柔和。

items.meaning: to portray in an image or words
items.example: The seal depicts a lion.
items.exampleCN: 这枚印章描绘一头狮子。

items.example: The pigment faded in the light.
The picture shows the harbour.

definition_zh: 水生的；水中生长的；与水有关的；水上运动的；（名词）水生生物
definition_en: living or growing in water, or connected with water, water environments and water sports
core_image: 睡莲的根扎在塘泥里，叶片浮出水面，水下的鱼在叶影间穿行
scene: 池塘里的睡莲把根扎在泥中，叶片浮在水面上。 Water lilies in the pond are aquatic plants that root in the mud and float on the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 aquatic 指「生长在水中的」（第 2 个义项：植物扎根水中或浮于水面）；句意：池塘里的睡莲是水生植物，根扎在泥里、叶浮在水面。图中可辨识物件：浮出水面的圆叶、塘底淤泥、游动的鱼、映着天光的池水。

pos.zh: 水生的；水中生长的；与水有关的；水上运动的
水生生物（常作复数 aquatics，指水生动植物或水上运动项目）

forms.label: 复数名词（水生生物／水上运动）

derivatives.zh: 水上运动项目；水生生物（总称）

senses.title: Animals that live in water
senses.definition: describing animals that spend their lives in water, whether fresh or salt
senses.definitionCN: 描述一生都在淡水或咸水中度过的动物
senses.example: Fish, turtles and frogs are aquatic animals with very different body plans.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼、龟和蛙都是水生动物，身体结构却大不相同。
senses.why: the Latin root aqua simply means water, so the adjective marks the medium an organism lives in rather than any particular body shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 aqua 就是「水」，因此这个形容词标记的是生物生活的介质，而不是某种特定体型。

senses.title: Plants that grow in or on water
senses.titleCN: 扎根水中或浮在水面的植物
senses.definition: describing plants that root in water or mud below water and may float their leaves at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 描述根扎在水中或水下泥里、叶片可浮到水面的植物
senses.example: Water lilies in the pond are aquatic plants that root in the mud and float on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里的睡莲是水生植物，根扎在泥里、叶浮在水面。
senses.why: botany extends the same medium-based label to plants, and the key contrast is with terrestrial, dry-land growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把同一个「按介质命名」的标签用于植物，关键对照是陆生的 dry-land 生长。

senses.title: Relating to water environments
senses.definition: connected with the physical or chemical conditions of rivers, lakes, wetlands and seas
senses.definitionCN: 与河流、湖泊、湿地和海洋的物理或化学条件有关
senses.example: The survey measured aquatic oxygen levels along the whole river.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了整条河的水体含氧量。
senses.why: once the word is detached from a particular organism it can describe any process or measurement whose setting is water.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词脱离具体生物，就可以描述任何以水为场景的过程或测量。

senses.title: Water sports and activities
senses.definition: connected with sports practised in or on water, such as swimming, rowing and diving
senses.definitionCN: 与在水中或水面上进行的运动有关，如游泳、划船和跳水
senses.example: The new centre hosts all aquatic events except open-water swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 新中心承办除公开水域游泳以外的全部水上项目。
senses.why: sports administration borrowed the adjective as a neutral cover term for events held in a pool or on a lake.
senses.whyCN: 体育管理借用这个形容词，作为在泳池或湖面上举行的项目的统称。

senses.title: A water-dwelling organism
senses.definition: a plant or animal that lives in water, often used in the plural for a collection of such organisms
senses.definitionCN: 生活在水中的植物或动物，复数常指一类水生生物的总称
senses.example: The reserve protects rare aquatics in the spring-fed pools.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区保护着这些泉水池中的珍稀水生生物。
senses.why: the noun is a straightforward conversion of the adjective, naming whatever the adjective describes.
senses.whyCN: 名词由形容词直接转化而来，指形容词所描述的那类事物。

senses.title: Kept in an aquarium
senses.definition: describing animals or plants kept in tanks for display or hobby use rather than in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 描述养在水箱中供展示或爱好之用、而非野生状态的动植物
senses.example: The shop sells aquatic supplies for both beginners and breeders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店为新手和繁殖者都提供水族用品。
senses.why: the hobby trade narrowed the adjective to tank-kept life, a smaller world that still shares the water medium.
senses.whyCN: 水族爱好把这个形容词收窄到水箱中的生物，范围更小，但介质仍是水。

senses.title: Of aquatic ecology as a field
senses.definition: used in ecology for studies of communities that live in water, as opposed to terrestrial ones
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中用于研究水中生物群落，与陆生群落相对
senses.example: Her thesis compares aquatic and terrestrial carbon cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文比较水生与陆生碳循环。
senses.why: the adjective became a standard term of division in ecology, pairing with terrestrial to split the living world by medium.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成为生态学的标准划分用语，与 terrestrial 配对，按介质把生物界一分为二。

senses.title: Rare figurative use: fluid and flowing
senses.titleCN: 罕见的修辞义：如水般流畅
senses.definition: rarely, describing movement or style that is smooth and flowing like water
senses.definitionCN: 罕见用法，形容动作或风格像水一样平滑流动
senses.example: Her aquatic grace on the beam surprised the judges.
senses.exampleCN: 她在平衡木上如水般的优雅让裁判惊讶。
senses.why: the metaphor is occasional and stylistic; dictionaries usually mark it as extended rather than a settled sense.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻只是偶发的修辞用法；词典通常把它标为引申用法，而非稳定义项。

intro.en: Aquatic comes from Latin aquaticus 'living in water', built on aqua 'water' plus the adjective suffix -aticus. It entered English in the early fifteenth century.
intro.cn: aquatic 来自拉丁 aquaticus「生活在水中的」，由 aqua「水」加形容词后缀 -aticus 构成，15 世纪初进入英语。

items.en: Aqua 'water' is one of the best-attested Latin nouns; its reconstructed Indo-European base is *akwa-, a form recovered by comparison rather than recorded anywhere.
items.cn: aqua「水」是拉丁语中记载最充分的名称之一；其重构的印欧语词根为 *akwa-，这一形式靠比较构拟，并无实际记录。

items.en: The suffix -aticus formed adjectives of place or belonging, so aquaticus meant 'of water, living in water'.
items.cn: 后缀 -aticus 构成表示场所或归属的形容词，因此 aquaticus 意为「水的、生活在水中的」。

items.en: English took the adjective in the early 1400s, at first in medical and natural-history writing about creatures and humours.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪初借入该形容词，最初见于医学与博物学著作，谈生物与体液。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries aquatic was applied to swimming, rowing and diving, giving the fixed phrase aquatic sports.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，aquatic 被用于游泳、划船与跳水，形成固定短语 aquatic sports。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology paired aquatic with terrestrial as the two basic media of life, turning the adjective into a technical division.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学把 aquatic 与 terrestrial 配对为两种基本生活介质，使该形容词成为技术分类用语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the *akwa- base is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：*akwa- 词根属重构形式，英语最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one separates aquatic from words built on the same aqua root but naming other things, and from one look-alike with a different root; group two contrasts it with neighbouring habitat terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 aquatic 与同出 aqua 词根却指别物的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照相邻的栖息地词语。

entries.definition: A printmaking technique that mimics washes of tone; it is built on Italian acqua tinta 'tinted water', so it shares aqua but names no living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 一种模仿水墨浓淡的版画技法；由意大利语 acqua tinta「染色之水」构成，与 aqua 同源，却并不指生物。

entries.definition: A rock layer that holds groundwater; Latin aqua plus ferre 'to carry', so the water root is shared but the referent is stone, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 储存地下水的地层；由拉丁 aqua 加 ferre「携带」构成，水词根相同，所指却是岩层而非生命。

entries.definition: The farming of fish, shellfish and water plants; aqua plus cultura 'cultivation', so it names an industry rather than a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 养殖鱼、贝类与水生植物；由 aqua 加 cultura「耕作」构成，指产业而非栖息地。

entries.definition: Hooked like an eagle's beak; it comes from Latin aquila 'eagle', not aqua 'water', so the resemblance is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 像鹰喙一样钩曲的；来自拉丁 aquila「鹰」而非 aqua「水」，因此形近并不同源。

entries.definition: Living in or relating to the sea; it is the salt-water half of aquatic and excludes rivers and lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在海中或与海有关的；它是 aquatic 的咸水一半，不含河流湖泊。

entries.definition: Living in or relating to non-salty inland water; it is the other half of aquatic, defined by low salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在淡水或与淡水有关的；是 aquatic 的另一半，以低盐度为界定。

entries.definition: Able to live both on land and in water; aquatic says one medium, amphibious adds the second.
entries.definitionCN: 能在陆地与水中两种环境生活；aquatic 只说一种介质，amphibious 则加上第二种。

entries.definition: Carried or spread by water, as a disease or a craft; it describes transport, not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 由水携带或传播的，如疾病或船只；它描述运输，而非栖息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real aqua root, real derivatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 aqua 词根、真实派生词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Aqua is Latin for water, and it survives in aquarium, aqueduct, aquifer and aquaculture.
normal.cn: aqua 是拉丁语的「水」，仍见于 aquarium、aqueduct、aquifer、aquaculture。

normal.en: The fixed pair aquatic / terrestrial divides life by medium in ecology textbooks.
normal.cn: 生态学教材用 aquatic / terrestrial 这一固定对立，按介质划分生命。

normal.en: Aquatic plants and aquatic animals are the two standard collocations in field guides.
normal.cn: aquatic plants 与 aquatic animals 是野外图鉴中的两个标准搭配。

normal.en: Aquatic sports is the administrative phrase for pool and lake events.
normal.cn: aquatic sports 是泳池与湖面赛事的行政管理用语。

normal.en: The noun aquatics names either water sports collectively or water-dwelling organisms.
normal.cn: 名词 aquatics 可指水上运动的总称，也可指水生生物。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf that lives half in air and half in water, its root never leaving the mud.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子一半在空气里、一半在水里，根始终不离开泥。

abstract.en: Picture a whole lake turned into a single room with its own weather.
abstract.cn: 想象整片湖被看成一间有自己天气的房间。

abstract.en: Picture a swimmer whose lines are so smooth that the water seems to move with her.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one medium: water. dict_mnemonic.text: elation ＝ e-（向外、向上，ex- 的变体）＋ lat（携带，拉丁 ferre／latus）＋ -ion（名词后缀）＝「被抬起来的状态」。情绪被抬高 → 兴高采烈、得意洋洋。同根换词尾：elate 动词「使兴奋」、elated 形容词「兴高采烈的」（人作主语：she was elated）、elatedly 副词、elating 形容词「令人兴奋的」（事作主语）。注意与 elation 押韵的 relation 也来自 latus（relatus 带回），但意思完全不同。近义梯度：elation 成功后的喜悦自豪；euphoria 强度更高的欣快（也用于医学）；exhilaration 带刺激感的振奋（运动、速度）；jubilation 公开表达的欢腾。反义方向是 dejection（de- 向下 ＋ ject 扔 ＝ 情绪被扔下去＝沮丧）。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、向上）＋ ferre（携带）→ efferre → elatus（被抬起的）→ elatio → elation（兴高采烈）
