pos.zh: 地理的；地理学的；地理位置的

senses.title: Relating to the discipline of geography
senses.definition: belonging to geography as a field of study, including its methods and concepts
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为研究领域的地理学，包括其方法与概念
senses.example: The paper applies geographic methods to the study of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文把地理学方法用于移民研究。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the discipline to a noun: geographic methods are the methods geography uses.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把学科附着到名词上：地理方法就是地理学所用的方法。

senses.title: Relating to physical location
senses.definition: concerning where a place or feature actually lies on the earth
senses.definitionCN: 关于某地或某要素在地球上的实际位置
senses.example: The two factories have the same geographic position but different markets.
senses.exampleCN: 两家工厂地理位置相同，市场却不同。
senses.why: Location is the field's most basic variable, so the adjective often answers the question 'where exactly?'
senses.whyCN: 位置是该学科最基本的变量，因此这个形容词常回答「究竟在哪里」。

senses.title: Spread across regions
senses.definition: distributed or varying across a territory rather than confined to one point
senses.definitionCN: 在一整片地域内分布或变化，而非局限于一点
senses.example: The team compared the crop yields of two geographic regions.
senses.exampleCN: 考察队比较了两个地理区域的作物产量。
senses.why: Once a phenomenon is mapped, it becomes a geographic pattern: differences arranged in space.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某现象被制图，它就成了地理格局：差异在空间中的排列。

senses.title: Of coordinates and map systems
senses.titleCN: 地理坐标与地图系统的
senses.definition: describing positions by latitude, longitude, or another earth-referenced grid
senses.definitionCN: 以纬度、经度或其它地球参照网格描述位置
senses.example: Geographic coordinates place the wreck within a few metres.
senses.exampleCN: 地理坐标把沉船位置精确到几米之内。
senses.why: A map needs a grid tied to the earth itself, and the adjective marks that earth-referenced system.
senses.whyCN: 地图需要一套绑定地球本身的网格，这个形容词标记的正是这种地球参照系统。

senses.title: Regional biological variation
senses.definition: differences among populations that arise from their separation in space
senses.definitionCN: 种群因空间分隔而产生的差异
senses.example: Geographic variation in wing length follows the winter temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 翅长的地理变异与冬季温度相关。
senses.why: Distance limits interbreeding, so space becomes a cause of biological difference.
senses.whyCN: 距离限制交配，因此空间本身成为生物差异的原因。

senses.title: Geographic isolation in evolution
senses.definition: separation of populations by distance, mountains, or water that blocks gene flow
senses.definitionCN: 因距离、山脉或水域阻断基因流而造成的种群分隔
senses.example: Geographic isolation split the bird into two species.
senses.exampleCN: 地理隔离把这种鸟分成两个物种。
senses.why: Speciation needs interrupted gene flow, and geography is the most common interruption.
senses.whyCN: 物种形成需要被中断的基因流，而地理是最常见的中断者。

senses.title: Commercial regional segmentation
senses.definition: relating to a market or service area defined by location
senses.definitionCN: 与按位置划定的市场或服务区域有关
senses.example: The company treats each province as a separate geographic market.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把每个省视为独立的地理市场。
senses.why: Business borrows the map to divide customers, so 'geographic' becomes a management category.
senses.whyCN: 企业借用地图来划分客户，于是「地理的」成为管理类别。

senses.title: Abstract: spatially organized
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：按空间组织起来的
senses.definition: arranged according to relative position, distance, or neighbourhood rather than by list order
senses.definitionCN: 按相对位置、距离或邻近关系而非列表顺序组织
senses.example: The archive is organized on a geographic principle, shelf by shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 档案按地理原则逐架排列。
senses.why: The metaphor extends the adjective from earth-space to any space in which nearness matters.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把形容词从地球空间扩展到任何「远近有意义」的空间。

intro.en: Geographic comes from Greek through Latin, the adjective of geography. Its elements are well recorded. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geographic 经拉丁语来自希腊语，是 geography 的形容词。其语素书证充分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ge meant 'earth'. Its deeper origin is uncertain and often treated as pre-Greek, so proposed roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: ge 意为「大地」。其更深来源不确定，常被视为前希腊语词，因此所提词根均属重构形式。

items.en: Graphikos meant 'of writing or drawing', from graphein 'to write'. Geographikos described what belongs to earth-writing.
items.cn: graphikos 意为「书写或描画的」，来自 graphein「写」。geographikos 指属于「书写大地」之物。

items.en: Late Latin geographicus borrowed the Greek adjective, and English took it as geographic.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 geographicus 借入这个希腊形容词，英语再借为 geographic。

items.en: The adjective expanded with exploration and cartography, attaching to maps, coordinates, and distributions.
items.cn: 这个形容词随探险与制图扩展，附着于地图、坐标与分布。

items.en: Twentieth-century terms such as geographic information system gave the word new technical homes; first dates for these compounds vary.
items.cn: 20 世纪的地理信息系统等术语为这个词提供了新的技术落点，这些复合词的首见年代各不相同。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns from the same Greek stock that are easily swapped; group two holds spatial adjectives with a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语词干、极易互换的形容词与名词；第二组是范围不同的空间形容词。

entries.definition: The longer adjective with the same meaning; British usage often prefers it, while American usage shortens it.
entries.definitionCN: 意义相同的较长形容词；英式常用它，美式则常用较短形式。

entries.definition: The discipline or a region's layout; geographic is the adjective that points back to it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科或地区布局；geographic 是指回它的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who practises geography; it is a noun, so it cannot modify another noun the way geographic does.
entries.definitionCN: 从事地理学的人；它是名词，不能像 geographic 那样修饰另一名词。

entries.definition: Relating to geology, the study of rocks; the ending -logic replaces -graphic and changes the field.
entries.definitionCN: 与地质学相关的；结尾 -logic 替换 -graphic，学科随之改变。

entries.definition: Relating to space in general, including rooms and layouts; geographic is tied specifically to the earth's surface.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指空间，包括房间与布局；geographic 特指地球表面。

entries.definition: Relating to a named region; it need not involve geographic analysis or coordinates.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一命名区域相关；不必涉及地理分析或坐标。

entries.definition: Relating to territory claimed or controlled by a state; it adds political control to mere location.
entries.definitionCN: 与国家主张或控制的领土有关；在单纯位置上叠加政治控制。

entries.definition: Relating to the detailed shape and elevation of the surface; geographic is wider and includes human patterns.
entries.definitionCN: 与地表详细形状和高程有关；geographic 范围更广，还包括人类格局。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real technical terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊语素、真实技术术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Geography is the noun; geographic is the adjective; geographically is the adverb.
normal.cn: geography 是名词，geographic 是形容词，geographically 是副词。

normal.en: Geographic distribution is the standard phrase for where a species occurs.
normal.cn: geographic distribution 是描述物种分布范围的标准短语。

normal.en: Geographic isolation is a standard cause of speciation.
normal.cn: 地理隔离是物种形成的标准成因。

normal.en: A geographic information system links data to coordinates.
normal.cn: 地理信息系统把数据与坐标关联起来。

normal.en: Do not confuse geographic with geologic: surface places versus deep rocks.
normal.cn: 不要把 geographic 与 geologic 混淆：前者是地表地方，后者是深部岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a colour that changes the moment you cross a border line.
abstract.cn: 想象一种颜色，越过边界线的瞬间就改变。

abstract.en: Picture two identical houses that behave differently because of where they stand.
abstract.cn: 想象两栋一模一样的房子，因所处位置不同而表现不同。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelved by distance instead of by title.
abstract.cn: 想象一座按距离而非书名排列的图书馆。

examples.en: The team compared the crop yields of two geographic regions.
examples.cn: 考察队比较了两个地理区域的作物产量。

examples.en: Geographic isolation allowed the island population to diverge.
examples.cn: 地理隔离使岛上种群得以分化。

examples.en: The map stores every record with geographic coordinates.
examples.cn: 地图用地理坐标存储每一条记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「geo（大地）+ graphic（描绘的）」——描绘大地的 → 地理的

root: 拉丁语 geographicus，来自希腊语 geographikos = ge「大地」+ graphein「书写、描画」+ -ikos「……的」。ge 更深来源不确定；graphein 词根清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from the academic field to location, regional distribution, coordinates, biological variation, isolation, market segmentation, and to any space-based order.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学术领域扩展到位置、区域分布、坐标、生物变异、隔离、市场划分，最后到任何以空间为依据的秩序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one map on which two distant regions are marked with the same symbol.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张地图上，两个相距很远的区域被标以相同符号。

branches.en: FIELD AND POSITION: the adjective can point to the discipline or to the simple fact of where something lies.
branches.cn: 学科与位置：这个形容词既可指学科，也可指某物所在的位置这一简单事实。

branches.en: DISTRIBUTION AND MARKET: mapping a phenomenon and dividing a market both turn space into a category.
branches.cn: 分布与市场：给现象制图与划分市场，都把空间变成分类依据。

branches.en: GRID: latitude and longitude tie every place to a common reference frame.
branches.cn: 网格：经纬度把每个地点绑定到共同参照系。

branches.en: DISTANCE AS CAUSE: separation produces variation and, eventually, new species.
branches.cn: 距离即原因：分隔产生变异，最终产生新物种。

branches.en: NEARNESS AS ORDER: any arrangement in which proximity matters can be called geographic.
branches.cn: 邻近即秩序：任何以远近为要义的排列都可称作地理的。

intro.en: The adjective is assembled from the same two Greek elements as the noun, plus an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由与名词相同的两个希腊语素加形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin geographicus and Greek geographikos stand behind the English adjective; ge and graphein are the ultimate elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 geographicus 与希腊语 geographikos 支撑这个英语形容词；ge 与 graphein 是最终语素。

items.example: Ge- marks earth-based sciences.
items.exampleCN: ge- 标记以大地为基础的科学。

items.example: -Graphic appears in geographic and photographic.
Geography is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: geography 是这个形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The study covers a wide geographic range.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究覆盖很广的地理范围。

items.example: Geographical names often preserve older languages.
items.exampleCN: 地名常保存更古老的语言。

items.example: The species is geographically split into two groups.
items.exampleCN: 该物种在地理上分为两个群体。

items.meaningCN: 研究地方的人；地理学家
items.example: A geographer prepared the regional atlas.
items.exampleCN: 一位地理学家编制了区域图集。

items.meaning: relating to geographic space and data
items.meaningCN: 地理空间的；与空间数据有关的
items.example: Geospatial data combine maps with statistics.
items.exampleCN: 地理空间数据把地图与统计结合。

latinEntries.structure: Late Latin geographicus, from Greek geographikos

definition_zh: 逐一列举；枚举；计数
definition_en: to mention or list things one by one in order
core_image: 演讲者竖起手指，一条一条把要点数到最后一根
scene: 报告逐条列出整改事项。 The report enumerates each corrective measure.
sceneCN: 这里 enumerate 是「逐一列举」（第 1 个义项：按顺序一条一条说出）；句意：报告逐条列出整改措施。

pos.zh: 逐一列举；枚举

senses.title: To list items one by one
senses.definition: to name each member of a set in order instead of summarising it
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序说出集合中每一个成员，而非笼统概括
senses.example: The witness enumerated the vehicles she saw.
senses.exampleCN: 证人把她见到的车辆逐一列出。
senses.why: The Latin stem is about number, so the verb treats a list as something counted item by item.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干与数目相关，因此动词把清单看作逐项计数的对象。

senses.title: To count or reckon up formally
senses.definition: to go through things so as to establish how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 逐件清点以确定数量
senses.example: Clerks enumerated the ballots overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 职员通宵清点选票。
senses.why: Older administrative use kept the arithmetic sense that the listing sense grew from.
senses.whyCN: 较早的行政用法保留了产生列举义的那层算术含义。

senses.title: To step through items in a program
senses.definition: in computing, to access the members of a data collection in sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域指按序访问数据集合的成员
senses.example: The loop enumerates every record in the table.
senses.exampleCN: 这段循环遍历表中的每条记录。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the word for the act of running through a list, keeping the one-by-one idea.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用该词表示跑完整个列表，保留逐条进行的含义。

intro.en: Enumerate joins a prefix of out to numerare, to number, from numerus, number.
intro.cn: enumerate 由表出的前缀加 numerare（计数）构成，numerus 意为数目。

items.en: Numerus means number, and numerare means to count.
items.cn: numerus 指数目，numerare 指计数。

items.en: Exnumerare shaped the compound with an out prefix.
items.cn: exnumerare 以表出的前缀塑成复合词。

items.en: Enumeratus names a thing counted through.
items.cn: enumeratus 指清点完毕之物。

items.en: English scholars take enumerate into formal prose.
items.cn: 十六世纪学者把 enumerate 带入正式书面语。

items.en: Statistics and law adopt enumeration as a technical noun.
items.cn: 十九世纪统计与法律采纳 enumeration 作技术名词。

items.en: Computing renews the verb for sequences of records.
items.cn: 现代英语中计算机领域让该动词在记录序列中复活。

note.en: Group one holds the numerus family; group two holds other verbs of listing.
note.cn: 第一组是 numerus 词族；第二组是其他列举动词。

entries.definition: The action noun used in statistics, law, and computing.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词，用于统计、法律与计算机。

entries.definition: Same stem with a negating prefix, meaning too many to count.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干加否定前缀，指多到数不清。

entries.definition: To put into numbers; the sense enumerate generalises.
entries.definitionCN: 使成数字，enumerate 将其义项泛化。

entries.definition: Sounds similar but means to flow out from a source.
entries.definitionCN: 读音相近但义为从源头流出。

entries.definition: The everyday way of writing items down in order.
entries.definitionCN: 按序写下条目的日常说法。

entries.definition: To set out each item separately, close in register.
entries.definitionCN: 逐条分列，语体接近。

entries.definition: To describe the parts fully, with less emphasis on order.
entries.definitionCN: 详尽描述各部分，较少强调顺序。

entries.definition: To record items in a fixed classification system.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定分类体系登记条目。

normalIntro.en: Inside enumerate sits numerate, so the verb is counting done out loud.
normalIntro.cn: enumerate 内含 numerate，因此这个动词是出声的计数。

normal.en: Use it when order matters: first, second, third.
normal.cn: 强调顺序时使用：第一、第二、第三。

normal.en: Enumerate is formal; list is neutral.
normal.cn: enumerate 正式，list 中性。

normal.en: The noun enumeration appears in reports and code names.
normal.cn: 名词 enumeration 常见于报告与代码命名。

normal.en: Avoid it for mere description; it demands countable items.
normal.cn: 不要用于单纯描述，它要求可数的条目。

normal.en: In code, enumerate a list to get index and value pairs.
normal.cn: 在代码中 enumerate 列表可同时得到序号与值。

abstract.en: Picture fingers rising one at a time as each item is named.
abstract.cn: 想象每说一条就竖起一根手指。

abstract.en: Imagine a clipboard checked line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象逐行核对的写字板清单。

abstract.en: Think of a clerk moving along a column of figures.
abstract.cn: 想想沿数字列逐行移动的办事员。

examples.en: She enumerated the risks without pausing.
examples.cn: 她毫不停顿地逐条列出风险。

examples.en: The manual enumerates the safety steps.
examples.cn: 手册逐条列出安全步骤。

examples.en: Please enumerate the items you need quoted.
examples.cn: 请逐一列出需要报价的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一纽美瑞特」——音近 enumerate，像把每纽美玉都数一遍，所以是逐一列举；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。」

root: 拉丁语 numerus（数目）→ numerare（计数）→ 过去分词 enumeratus → 英语 enumerate，核心义「一项一项数出来」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb runs from counting objects, to naming items in order, to stepping through data in code.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从清点实物，到按序命名条目，再到代码中遍历数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger raised for each item until the list is spent.
core.cn: 核心意象：每说一条竖起一根手指，直到数完。

branches.en: Listing in words is the common prose sense.
branches.cn: 用语言逐条列出是最通行的散文义。

branches.en: Counting keeps the arithmetic root alive.
branches.cn: 清点实物让算术词根保持活力。

branches.en: Code formalises the sequence as an operation.
branches.cn: 代码把序列固化为一项操作。

branches.en: Both require discrete countable items.
branches.cn: 两者都要求分立可数的对象。

branches.en: Prose and program both walk a list end to end.
branches.cn: 书面语与程序都从头到尾走完列表。

intro.en: A Latin numeral stem takes verbal and nominal endings through two learned layers.
intro.cn: 拉丁数词词干经两层书面借用取得动词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin Numerus means number, numerare to count, and enumeratus counted out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 指数目，numerare 指数数，enumeratus 指已数出。

items.example: E- marks counting out.
items.exampleCN: e- 标记数出这一动作。

Numerare supplies the action.
The ending forms enumerate.
Common in legal writing.
It yields enumeration.

items.exampleCN: 基于该词干的现代新词。
